title: us-911-commission: chapter 1's opening paragraphs live on the 'preface' section page
description: Found writing the 0z1o post (2026-10-03). On production, /reports/us-911-commission?p=tuesday-september-11-2001-dawned redirects to /reports/us-911-commission/preface?..., and the preface page renders the h2 "WE HAVE SOME PLANES" plus chapter 1's two opening paragraphs before 1.1. Sections split at ### (1.1, 1.2 ...), so text between a chapter ## heading and its first ### falls into the previous section. Likely affects every chapter intro in 9/11 and possibly other reports with ##/### nesting. Fix: a chapter intro should belong to its chapter (own section or the first subsection). Expect section slugs/ids to move; aliases cover ids.
notes:
Supervisor 2026-10-03: live regression risk from the 9/11 hybrid (ivg.1): chapter openings filed under the previous section. Check whether Saville (ivg.2, #249) has the same cause before it ships in a94n. 2026-10-03 agent: ROOT CAUSE is ingest splitSections (src/sections.ts), not cleanEdition's levels (## chapter, ### N.N are right). title: Renderer pairs sparse references to repeated note labels wrongly; no check sees it (Litvinenko 20, Philip Morris 17 of 19, Leveson 132 of 260 before b94)
description: resolveNoteReferences pairs references to definitions by an LCS over labels. Where few of a chapter's references are linked, the LCS has many equal-length solutions and picks early definitions: measured by pairing as the renderer does and comparing each definition's PDF page with its reference's page, Litvinenko renders 20 of 756 sidenotes from another page, Philip Morris 17 of 19, Leveson (before b94) 132 of 260, PSI 18, Lehman 3, Chilcot 3. note-marker-wrong-note cannot catch this: it takes the same LCS as the truth. b94's layoutMarkers fixes it for the four reports that declare it (all 0) by making references dense; Litvinenko (756 -> 802 references, 0 from another page) and Philip Morris (19 -> 21, 0) measured in memory with layoutMarkers() and flushFootnoteMarkers dropped. Fix: declare layoutMarkers in Litvinenko and Philip Morris (owners), and add a quality/oracle signal that compares a rendered note's page with its marker's page (IngestResult knows both: footnotes carry pdfIndex, blocks carry at).
notes: 2026-10-03 (agent): note-off-page oracle signal (ingest PR stacked on #46) + budgets; layoutMarkers() declared in uk-litvinenko-inquiry and us-v-philip-morris. Off-page 20 -> 0 and 17 -> 0; see PRs.

title: Design: annotation format for things we add to the text (page numbers, paragraph numbers, ids, provenance, corrections): inline syntax vs. sidecar file
description: Rufus, 2026-10-03: we need a sidecar format or inline annotations in markdown for what we add: printed page anchors (today an inline %%page N%% comment), paragraph ids and printed paragraph numbers, aliases (now reports/<id>/aliases.yaml), corrections (corrections.yaml), fidelity flags (fidelity.md), source provenance per block (clean edition vs. PDF), editorial marks/highlights, and the page-label scheme (b78.10). Questions: what stays inline in full.md (readable, diffable, travels with the text) vs. a sidecar keyed by paragraph id (keeps the text clean, allows many layers, like W3C Web Annotation or a standoff format); stability when ids move (aliases); tooling (markdown-it/remark plugins, c0h); a spec others could reuse. Survey prior art (CommonMark attribute syntax {#id}, Pandoc attributes, MyST roles, CriticMarkup, standoff annotation in TEI, W3C Web Annotation, hypothes.is anchoring). Output: docs/design/<date>-annotation-format.md with a recommendation and a migration plan. Opus.
notes: 2026-10-03 (Opus agent): design doc docs/design/2026-10-03-annotation-format.md; decision 0002 set to proposed (option D: inline %%page%% milestones allowed mid-paragraph; locators in front matter; generated blocks.jsonl ledger with ids/pages/provenance; human layers standoff with one anchor model id+TextQuote, resolved id->aliases->quote->orphan; W3C export). title: [epic] Report preparation pipeline: one skill per stage, from finding sources to promotion
description: Rufus, 2026-10-03: plan a preparation pipeline with skills, for each report: (1) source: find good-quality versions as well as the original (clean HTML/XML, tagged PDFs, Wikisource, EPUB, court text, publisher originals; see docs/research/better-source-texts.md and its sourcing checklist e5dv); (2) cache those and prepare the report repo (pinned SHA-256s, licences, reference/, manifest); (3) propose: a first ingest (hybrid cleanEdition where a clean source exists, otherwise the PDF pipeline with chosen passes); (4) evaluate and refine (quality signals and budgets, the oracle, golden pages, adjudicated page breaks, pnpm score, ingest try; the improvement loop, 38s); (5) introduction, highlights and excerpts (the report-introduction skill exists), perhaps before publishing; (6) publish (pnpm ship: preflight, publish, deploy, reindex, verify; aliases); (7) announce (changelog/blog post, launch thread); (8) promote (excerpt campaign; y2t, pnpm posts). Each stage is a skill in .claude/skills/<stage>/SKILL.md with entry and exit criteria, the commands, the checks that gate the next stage, the model to use (Sonnet/Opus), and the artefacts it hands on. The supervisor runs reports through stages; one owning agent per report per stage. Builds on docs/report-preparation.md (s9b), docs/report-pipeline.md, AGENTS.md section D, docs/release-checklist.md and docs/design/lessons.md.

title: Research: can we get better source texts than 'bad PDFs'? Sourcing strategy for current and future reports
description: Rufus, 2026-10-02: the question deserves its own bead and a detailed write-up (almost a blog post). 38s.1 inventoried clean editions for the 13 live reports (docs/design/reference-editions.md); ivg builds the hybrid path that uses them. This bead is the general question, for every report including future ones: where do better sources come from, and how do we get them? Lines to research: (1) publishers' originals: Word/ODT/InDesign/XML from inquiry secretariats, government publishers (TSO, GPO), law firms (Jenner & Block), courts; who to ask and how (FOI/FOIA requests, archives, direct email); success stories. (2) Structured government data: govinfo bulk XML (USLM, GPO), the UK National Archives web archive and legislation.gov.uk-style XML, Hansard, congressional record. (3) Court records: CourtListener/RECAP, Caselaw Access Project, PACER docket text. (4) Web editions: official HTML, Wayback captures, accessibility versions (Easy Read, large print, screen-reader editions often have clean text), EPUB/Kindle editions (e.g. the 9/11 Commission Report's trade editions). (5) Better extraction of the PDFs we have: tagged-PDF structure, pdftohtml layout, ML layout models (Docling, Marker, and the like), a modern OCR re-run for scans (Challenger, Jack Smith), and vision-LLM transcription with PDF-anchored verification. (6) Crowd or partner sources: Wikisource, Project Gutenberg, academic projects, archive.org texts. For each: coverage across our live and queued reports, fidelity and version risk, licence, effort and cost. Output: docs/research/better-source-texts.md (blog-quality prose with a recommendation and a per-report sourcing table, including queued reports: Duelfer, Valukas volumes, Chilcot volumes, Saville volumes) plus follow-up beads (e.g. specific requests to send to publishers; Rufus sends any outward request himself).
notes: 2026-10-03 research done: PR #229 (https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter/pull/229), docs/research/better-source-texts.md plus experiment files. Findings: 12 of 14 source PDFs are born-digital, so their words are already exact. Only Challenger (1986 scan) and Jack Smith (copier scan) are OCR. What we need from a better source is structure. New sources: Wikisource has page-aligned proofread text of 9/11 (310 proofread + 40 validated of 362 pages) and the Chilcot executive summary (142/150). GPO published a Deep Water EPUB in 2011, the only structured edition of Deepwater. Queued reports: Chilcot volumes on gov.uk are untagged but the inquiry-site section PDFs are tagged; Valukas Vol 5 exists redacted and unredacted (docket 8307/8366); Saville HTML covers all 10 volumes. Dead ends: govinfo XML/HTML (PDF only for our packages), Project Gutenberg, IA mirrors. Experiment, 4 scanned pages against hand ground truth: our OCR layer gets 0.3-1.4% of words wrong. tesseract gets 0-0.9% wrong but is worse on footnote markers. Docling layout + Apple Vision dropped lines on Challenger (16-22%). granite-docling VLM gets 0-1.6% wrong (2 misreads in ~1,600 words), reads markers almost perfectly and gives structure, at 80-100 s/page on an M4 CPU. Recommendation: per-report source stacks, with words from the best text, structure from HTML/EPUB/tags/verified VLM, and anchors from the PDF. Do the cheap wins now. Use a verified VLM structure pass for the scans. Send the six drafted requests (Appendix A, Rufus sends) but plan as if none succeed. Add a sourcing checklist for new reports. New beads: 7d4y, egsa, kyj3, e693, 6nkk, e5dv. Notes appended to 0a7, wdt, 94u, d0h. Also corrected 38s.1: the Valukas PDFs are born-digital, not scans.
close_reason: docs/research/better-source-texts.md (site #229); follow-ups 7d4y, egsa, kyj3, e693, 6nkk, e5dv.

title: Paragraph-id aliases: keep ?p= links resolving when paragraphs merge or are renamed (joins, hybrid sources, corrections)
description: Ids keep moving as the pipeline improves: 38s.10's joins merged Jack Smith 'trump-has-something-else-left' into 'just-before-2-24-p' (it was in a highlight, a share card and the posting queue, so already-posted links break), plus Lehman and Philip Morris editorial ids; apk renamed a 9/11 id; the hybrid sources (ivg) will move most ids for 9/11, Saville, Hillsborough and Duelfer. Add a per-report alias map (old id -> new id), generated automatically by the integrator from pnpm corpus check's moved-id diff (match by text containment: an old fragment contained in a new paragraph), served so ?p=<old> redirects to the new id and section. Add a check that every id ever published (record them) still resolves. Coordinate with ivg.1, which is designing id migration for the 9/11 hybrid. Sonnet.
notes:
From ivg.1 (9/11 hybrid): proposed shape, implemented as data only: report repo aliases.yaml {aliases: {old-id: new-id}, unmatched: [old-id]} (us-911-commission#9: 212 aliases, 125 unmatched), generated by text containment (old paragraph's first 12/8/6/4 normalised words found exactly once in the new text stream -> the id of the paragraph holding that position; fallback: 8 words from its middle; script: hyb worktree score-out/hyb/ids.ts, worth promoting to scripts/aliases.mjs). Serving is cheap: aggregate copies aliases.yaml like PROCESSING.md, prerender adds meta.paragraphAliases, and the /reports/:id route resolves meta.paragraphToSection[p] ?? paragraphToSection[aliases[p]] and redirects with p=<new>&h kept (h= text quotes survive because the text did not change). Section slugs moved too (appendix-b-table-of-names-us-officials -> appendix-b-table-of-names): a section alias map in the same file would cover them. Regenerate against what is live at deploy, not against the branch base.
Correction to the ivg.1 note: the generator is now committed as the site's scripts/aliases.ts (PR #228); 9/11 counts with it: 209 aliases, 128 unmatched.
PR opened from branch q8c-aliases; see PR. Not closed (integrator closes on ship).

Proposed follow-up (0002): resolve an id directly, then via aliases, then by quotation search; anything still unmatched fails a check. Consider before freezing ids (0002 open question 3).

title: ingest: layout-gated page-break join pass (first-line indent + justified full line), rules R1/R2 from 38s.8
description: From 38s.8 (docs/design/2026-10-02-learning-from-aligned-pairs.md §4, §7). Rules: join a page-break pair when the previous line is unfinished and the next line is flush with the line under it on the same page (|first-line indent| < 0.6 em) or opens lower case, does not open on a label (57. (b) 9.88 •), and font/size do not change; also when the previous line ends a sentence but the page is justified, that line reaches the right margin (< 0.5 em) and the next is flush, unlabelled, same font, > 4 words. Measured: page-break accuracy dev 84.7% -> 95.6%, held-out 80.8% -> 88.9% (R2 93.3% vs adjudicated labels on a random held-out sample); PM all-line-break accuracy 98.57% -> 99.48%. Needs per-line layout (left, width, font, size) in ingest: reuse the pdftohtml -xml parse of the b78.5 layout oracle (src/lib/score/layout.ts in the site already parses it). Opt-in per report first; measure every report with pnpm score and pnpm quality before making it default. title: Learn from aligned pairs: mine PDF-vs-clean alignments for the decisions the pipeline gets wrong, derive rules, features or models for PDF-only reports
description: Once the scorer aligns pipeline output to clean editions (38s.2), every aligned report becomes labelled data. For each block-level decision the pipeline makes, the alignment gives the right answer. Decisions include: join across a page break or not; prose vs. block quotation; heading or body (and level); footnote marker or number; furniture or text; list item or paragraph. 1) Build a labelled dataset: one row per decision point, with its layout features (pdftohtml -xml font, size, position, indent, page position; text shape: ending punctuation, next-line case, quote marks, length; neighbouring blocks) and the label from the clean edition. 2) Error analysis: which decisions fail most, in which layout contexts, and which features separate right from wrong (the 'what to look for' in PDF-only reports). 3) Try learned deciders against the hand-written passes on held-out reports: a small interpretable model (decision tree or logistic regression, whose splits read as rules a pass can adopt), and an LLM referee given few-shot examples drawn from this dataset for ambiguous blocks only. Measure accuracy, cost and transfer to reports from other publishers and layouts (UK inquiry vs. US commission vs. court opinion). 4) Recommend: hand rules informed by the data, a learned decider inside a pass, or a model referee, per decision type. Also turn the hardest real examples into fixtures for the synthetic benchmark (38s.4). Opus for design and analysis.

title: [epic] Get better faster: reference texts, scoring and an improvement loop for the pipeline
description:
Rufus, 2026-10-02: the point of integrator and research sessions is not only to fix bugs but to learn how we get better faster. Bugs keep getting through. A root cause: we have no clean reference text to score the pipeline's output against, so every improvement is judged by agents reading pages and by regex signals (b78.2) that only find shapes we already know. With reference texts we could score each pass change (paragraph boundaries, headings, block types, footnote links, character accuracy), develop techniques against a number instead of anecdotes, and find the next defect class automatically.

This epic is the research programme for that. It complements b78 (the harness): b78 catches regressions and known defect classes; this epic builds ground truth and a scoring/improvement loop, and asks whether parts of the pipeline should change.

Research lines (child beads):
1. Reference-edition inventory: which reports already exist as clean independent text (official HTML, govinfo/GPO XML, court opinion text, Hansard-style HTML, tagged-PDF structure trees). Free ground truth we are not using.
2. Alignment scorer: align our output to a reference edition and produce structural metrics per report.
3. Vision-model gold pages: can a model transcribing page images produce gold text good enough to score against (measured on reports where a reference edition exists)? If yes, gold for every report is cheap.
4. Synthetic benchmark: PDFs generated from known markdown with report-like layouts (footnotes, running heads, page-break splits, block quotes, small caps, side banners, two columns): unlimited perfectly labelled pages.
5. Extractor bake-off: tagged-PDF structure, pdftohtml layout, ML layout extractors (Docling, Marker and the like), vision LLM vs. our pipeline, scored by line 2.
6. Improvement loop: dev/held-out split across reports so heuristics don't overfit, automatic error clustering ranked by reader impact, score deltas in every release, and a short "what slowed us / what would have caught it" retro from every integrator and fix agent.
7. Synthesis: a design doc recommending the improvement architecture, once 1-2 have results.
notes: Rufus, 2026-10-02: reports with a clean edition are the training ground for reports without one. Decision: even where a clean edition becomes the served source, keep running the PDF pipeline on that report as a shadow ingest, scored against the clean text. Those reports form the labelled corpus: the dev set for developing passes, a held-out set for checking them, and the source of learned rules and examples for PDF-only reports (Jack Smith, Duelfer, Valukas, probably Leveson). See the learning bead (38s.8).

title: Quality harness 3: golden pages — per-report golden.yaml verified against the PDF, checked by pnpm ingest verify
description:
Golden pages against the PDF (plan §3.2). The regex signals (b78.2) say "this looks wrong"; nothing says "this page is right". Add per-report ground truth: `golden.yaml` in each report repo, checked by `pnpm ingest verify`, so a pass change that breaks a page the catalogue cares about fails immediately, and so signal precision can be measured against something.

Format (`<report-repo>/golden.yaml`):
```
pages:
  - pdf: 42            # PDF page index, volume 1 unless `volume:` given
    printed: 34
    verified_by: "agent, 2026-10-05, against the page image"
    paragraphs: 5      # body paragraphs that START on this page (not continuations)
    continues_previous: true   # the page opens mid-paragraph
    headings: ["3. The decision to take the UN route"]
    quotes: 1
    footnotes: [12, 13, 14]    # note numbers defined on this page
    markers: [12, 13, 14]      # markers referenced on this page
    must_contain: ["suffering from abdominal pain, profuse diarrhoea and vomiting for two days"]   # one paragraph contains this exact run (spanning the former split)
    must_not_be_quote: ["vomiting for two days"]
```
Check: regenerate the report in memory (as `pnpm ingest check` does), locate the page's blocks via `%%page%%` markers / block page attribution, assert each field; report per page `✓/✗` with the first mismatch. Allow a `tolerance:` for `paragraphs` (±1) where the page has ambiguous sub-items.

Scope for this bead: 13 reports × 5 pages = 65 pages, chosen from the catalogue's concrete examples (each class A–N has at least one page), plus one ordinary page per report. Verification is by an agent reading the PDF page image (pdftoppm -f N -l N -png) against the YAML it writes; Rufus spot-checks a sample. Record the agent and date in `verified_by`. A golden page is edited only when the PDF reading says the previous entry was wrong, with the reason in the commit message.

Also: a CLI `pnpm ingest golden <id> <pdfPage>` that prints the page's text layer and the pipeline's current blocks for it side by side, to make writing an entry a two-minute job.
acceptance_criteria: golden.yaml exists in all 13 report repos with ≥ 5 verified pages each covering every catalogue class at least once across the corpus; pnpm ingest verify checks them and fails on a deliberately broken regeneration (e.g. removing quoteInset(3) from Litvinenko); pnpm ingest golden <id> <page> prints the side-by-side view.
notes:
b78.5 retro (2026-10-02): build the golden pages and a page inspection kit together. 'pnpm ingest page <id> <vol> <pdfPage>' prints the layout lines (indentEm, rightGapEm, font, label) beside the produced blocks; '--fixture <name>' writes a test fixture from it. Golden pages = these fixtures with expected per-page oracle counts, so every oracle or pass change gets a precision number. title: Quality harness 1: pnpm quality check — corpus signals with per-report budgets, in verify.sh
description: First layer of the quality harness (docs/design/2026-10-02-quality-harness-plan.md §3.1; catalogue §3 for every class and its live counts). Build `pnpm quality check` in the site repo: a set of pure signal functions over each report's `reports//full.md` and pre-rendered `assets/generated/reports//{full-body.html,meta.json}`, counted per report, compared with a per-report budget in `reports/quality-budget.yaml`, failing verify.sh when any count exceeds its budget. Day one, budgets equal today's counts (verify stays green); every fix ratchets them down (b78.3). Files: `src/lib/quality/signals.ts` (one exported function per signal, `(input: QualityInput) => Finding[]` where `QualityInput = { markdown: string; html: string; meta: Meta }` and `Finding = { signal, page: number|null, excerpt: string }`), `src/lib/quality/index.ts` (`measure(input): Record`), `scripts/quality.mjs` (`check | report | ratchet`), `tests/quality.test.ts`, `reports/quality-budget.yaml`, a `quality` script in package.json, a step in `scripts/verify.sh` after "Corpus blast radius". Move `src/lib/density.ts`'s check into the same module as the signal `ids-per-1k-words` (keep its threshold semantics as a floor budget), keep its test. Block model: split the markdown (front matter stripped) on blank lines into blocks; classify by first char: heading `#`, quote `> `, list `- `, note `[^N]:`, page marker `%%page N%%`, table `|`, otherwise prose. `endsSentence(text)`: trailing `[.?!:;]` then optional closing quotes/brackets then zero or more of linked markers `[^N]`, bare 1-3 digit markers, or `*`. Strip `[^N]` before pattern matching. Reuse `pageBreakSplits` and `endsSentence` from `@rtm/ingest` where exported rather than re-implementing. Signals (v1), with the catalogue class and today's corpus total so the implementer can check the port against the numbers: 1. `severed-into-quote` (A): prose block not ending a sentence, next block (skipping page markers) is a quote opening lower-case or `,;)` without an opening quotation mark. Today 843 same-page + 354 across a page break. Record whether a page marker was crossed. 2. `severed-paragraph` (B/C): same but the next block is prose opening lower-case/`,;)`; today 289 same-page + 26 across. Also `severed-paragraph-capital` (across a page break only, next block opens on a capital; today 959) as a separate, non-gated "advisory" signal with no budget until precision is measured (b78.6). 3. `bare-footnote-marker` (F): in prose and quote blocks after stripping `[^N]`, regex `/[a-z\)”"’][.,;:!?][1-9]\d{0,2}(?=\s+[A-Z“"]|$)/gm`. Today 9,032 (Leveson 6,394; Hillsborough 450 with 6 definitions). Also report `bare / (bare + definitions)` as a percentage in `report`. 4. `note-text-in-body` (E): prose block opening `/^\d{1,3}\s+(?:[A-Z]|See\b|Id\.|Ibid)/` (not a month/year), or opening `/^(Ibid|Id\.|See,? (e\.g\.,? )?(supra|id\.|[A-Z])|Cf\.|Supra|Testimony of|Interview with|Hearing Exhibit)/`. Today 121 + 80. Optional per-report `citationVocabulary` list in the budget file (the 626 technique: `SCO-`, `GS MBS-E`, `Hearing Exhibit`) counted as a third sub-signal where declared. 5. `furniture-paragraph` (K): a prose block of ≤ 8 words whose lower-cased text recurs ≥ 4 times in the report; count every occurrence (Litvinenko today: `The Litvinenko Inquiry` ×132, `Part N | Chapters…` ×109; Challenger `findings` ×55 etc. which is class I but the same signal). 6. `contents-entry-without-heading` (I): list items of the shape `- Title — N` (or dot leaders then N); normalise (lower-case, strip punctuation and leading numbering) and look for a heading whose normalised text equals or ends with it; report the count and the ratio to entries. Today 1,908 / 2,884. Budget on the count. 7. `heading-plausibility` (H/I): headings per 100 pages outside [3, 60] → one finding; heading text repeated ≥ 3 times; heading ending in a function word (`of|the|and|to|in|for|a|an|on|by|with|or|at`); heading containing `[^N]`; heading longer than 14 words. Count each. 8. `printed-page-reversal` (K): consecutive `%%page N%%` markers where N decreases (today 18; Challenger 14). 9. `rendered-h1` (N): `…` as % of `meta.words` (Lehman 42.8%, PSI 14.6%). `ids-per-1k-words` (J, existing floor 4). 10. `quote-share` (D): quote blocks / (quote + prose) overall and by printed-page parity; budget the absolute difference between parities (Deepwater pre-fix would have been ~90 points; today ≤ 2 everywhere). Budget file shape: `reports/quality-budget.yaml` → `reports: { : { : , … } }` plus a top-level `defaults` block used for a report with no entry (a new report): default = the corpus median rate per 1k words × the report's words, rounded up, so a new ingest cannot ship above the corpus's typical level. `pnpm quality check` prints one line per report (✓/✗ with `signal: count/budget` for every exceeded signal and the first three excerpts with page numbers) and exits 1 on any failure. `pnpm quality report` prints the full per-report × per-signal table (markdown) with budget and delta columns. `pnpm quality ratchet []` rewrites budgets down to the current counts, never up; raising a budget is a hand edit with a `# why: ` comment on the line, and `check` fails if a budget was raised without a comment (compare against git HEAD's copy of the file). Tests (vitest): each signal gets fixtures cut from the live corpus examples in the catalogue (the Litvinenko 3.120 severed quote; `impartial.15 I underline` and `by it.3 Given`; Chilcot `Security Sector Reform 884. An SSR…`; Litvinenko `Part 3 | Chapters 1 to 5 | Alexander Litvinenko` ×5; Challenger `94 → 2`; Columbia `# 18-7503-005` rendered as h1) and a clean counter-example each. Rule from AGENTS.md: run every signal against the broken text and watch it fail before trusting it. Do not change any report, pass or pin in this bead. Peer noise: `pnpm ingest check` currently fails for us-lehman-examiner and us-v-philip-morris, and `pnpm ingest verify` for uk-saville-inquiry, from other agents' uncommitted work; this check must read `reports//full.md` as aggregated, so it is unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm quality check runs in verify.sh and is green on today's corpus with reports/quality-budget.yaml at today's counts; every v1 signal has a vitest fixture cut from a catalogue example that fails on the broken text; pnpm quality report prints the per-report table; corpus totals within 5% of the catalogue's (severed-into-quote ~843+354, bare-footnote-marker ~9,032, contents-entry-without-heading ~1,908, furniture-paragraph Litvinenko ~241).

title: uk-chilcot-inquiry: 892 numbered paragraphs render as <ol><li> with no id — only 60 of ~950 paragraphs citable
description:
The Chilcot Executive Summary's numbered paragraphs reach full.md as '13. To do so…', which Markdown reads as an ordered list: each renders as
  1. with no paragraph id. assets/generated/reports/uk-chilcot-inquiry/full-body.html has 60

    (vs 1,800–12,000 on comparable inquiries); almost the whole body, including every conclusion (e.g. para 20 'the diplomatic options had not at that stage been exhausted', para 432 legal basis 'far from satisfactory'), cannot be cited, quoted in an introduction, highlighted or linked. Found writing the introduction (reportsthatmatter-rcz.1), which it blocks. Fix direction: numberedFindings() already escapes '3437\. ' for Philip Morris, but only recognises lines indented past the margin; Chilcot's numbers sit at the margin, so adding numberedFindings() to uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts changes nothing (tried, full.md identical). Either make numberedParagraphs() (opt-in, used by Chilcot, Leveson, Hillsborough, Litvinenko, Saville) also write its paragraphs as 'N\. ' in blocksToMarkdown, or let numberedFindings accept margin-set numbers. Beware: the same '^N. ' lines exist in Litvinenko (111), Leveson (320), Hillsborough (384), Challenger (343) — gaining ids there may shift -2 dedupe suffixes on existing ids, so run the corpus check. Also: headings fused into the first numbered paragraph ('Introduction 1. In 2003…', 'Negotiation of resolution 1441 119. …') — see reportsthatmatter-ixe. No existing check caught this: a 'share of body text in

  2. without id' or 'paragraph ids per 1,000 words' check would.
close_reason:
Fixed and shipped. Root cause: numberedParagraphs() correctly split Chilcot's margin-set "N." lines into their own paragraph blocks, but blocksToMarkdown() only escaped a paragraph's leading number when block.finding was set (numberedFindings, indented findings like Philip Morris) — a margin-set numbering had no such tag, so every one of Chilcot's 892 numbered paragraphs reached Markdown as a bare "20. …", which Markdown reads as an ordered-list item with no id.

Fix: new opt-in pass escapeNumberedParagraphs() in @rtm/ingest (v0.14.1), declared alongside numberedParagraphs() only in uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts; pipeline() rejects it if declared without numberedParagraphs. Litvinenko, Leveson, Hillsborough and Challenger also have "^N. " lines but don't declare it — pnpm corpus check confirms only Chilcot moved (13/13 checked, 12 byte-identical).

Citable paragraphs: 64 -> 956 (all 892 numbered paragraphs now carry an id, e.g. #20-inquiry-s-view-diplomatic and #432-circumstances-which-ultimately-decided — text-derived, never positional, same convention as Philip Morris's findings).

Added a corpus-wide invariant check that would have caught this on day one: paragraph ids per 1,000 words (src/lib/density.ts, MIN_PARAGRAPH_IDS_PER_1000_WORDS = 4), wired into `pnpm corpus check` unconditionally. Fails on the pre-fix numbers (1.07/1000), passes on the fix (15.52/1000) and every other current report (floor 6.73/1000, jack-smith-vol1). Test: tests/density.test.ts. Noted on reportsthatmatter-b78.

title: [bug] jack-smith-vol1 the-results-of-the-investigation: paragraphs split mid-sentence at page breaks, one continuation set as a block quotation (GH jack-smith-report#1)
description:
Reported by Rufus 2026-09-26: https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/jack-smith-report/issues/1 — page https://reportsthatmatter.org/reports/jack-smith-vol1/the-results-of-the-investigation.

Examples from the screenshots:
1. '...The throughline of all of Mr. Trump's criminal efforts was deceit-knowingly false claims of election' / new paragraph 'fraud-and the evidence shows that Mr. Trump used these lies...' — severed mid-phrase at printed p.3/4; continuation starts lowercase.
2. '...Mr. Trump also monitored legal developments' / new paragraph 'regarding the election and was on notice...' — severed mid-sentence, lowercase continuation.
3. '...could not have believed the specific fraud claims that they were' / block quotation 'making because the numbers they touted...Mr. Trump privately' / new paragraph 'acknowledged sounded "crazy"...' — one sentence broken into three blocks across p.5/6, the middle set as a quote (same skew/inset cause as kb4).

A paragraph ending without terminal punctuation followed by a paragraph/quote starting lowercase is almost always a page-break split. Fix in the pipeline (join across page break when previous ends mid-sentence and next starts lowercase or continues the sentence; treat a page-opening inset that continues a mid-sentence paragraph as continuation), never by hand in full.md. Measure corpus-wide before/after.
acceptance_criteria: All three examples read as continuous prose on the live page; corpus-wide count of (no terminal punctuation → lowercase-start paragraph/quote) pairs reported before and after; ingest check diffs understood; verify.sh passes.
notes:
2026-09-28 fix (unreleased). Two causes. (1) mergeAcrossPages looked past only ONE page marker. A paragraph filling a whole page leaves that page's marker behind it, so examples 1 and 2 (%%page 3#2%% %%page 4#2%%; %%page 5%% %%page 6%%) were never joined. (2) Skew-inset page openings arrive as quote blocks, which were never joined (example 3). Why no check caught it: severedSentenceCheck compares only the immediately next block (a page marker hides the split), counts quotes only, and is a 20% rate gate. Fix: opt-in pass pageBreakContinuations() plus a measure, pageBreakSplits(markdown), in ingest PR reportsthatmatter/ingest#15. Jack Smith declares it in jack-smith-report#2. title: A numbered paragraph opener ("3.77 ") doesn't start a new paragraph when no blank line separates it from the one before
description:
Confirmed live in production: uk-litvinenko-inquiry/chapter-2-leaving-russia (https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/uk-litvinenko-inquiry/issues/2) shows paragraphs 3.77-3.81 -- five distinct numbered paragraphs -- all fused into one

, and 3.75+3.76 fused into another, on the same page where 3.82 onward render correctly, one per paragraph. Root cause, confirmed against the raw pdftotext -layout output: this report's own typesetting is inconsistent about whether a blank line separates consecutive numbered paragraphs. Where 3.82, 3.83, 3.84... have a real blank line between them, toBlocks correctly starts a fresh paragraph at each. Where 3.75-3.81 have NO blank line (each numbered opener sits flush against the previous paragraph's last line, both at indent 0 -- the "hanging indent" numbering style these reports use puts the number at the margin and the paragraph's own text one tab-stop in, matching ordinary continuation lines), nothing distinguishes the numbered opener from a continuation line, so it silently welds on. @rtm/ingest src/paragraphs.ts already has a function for exactly this number style -- opensNumberedParagraph(text), matching "7.1", "10.14", per its own comment "the paragraph numbering these reports run throughout" (plural — this convention isn't unique to Litvinenko) -- but it is used in exactly one place (the division-heading-continuation guard, line ~540) and never consulted by toBlocks' own startsParagraph decision, which is indent-only: const startsParagraph = !quoted[i] && indent > margin + 1; A numbered opener at indent 0 never clears margin+1, so it can never trigger a paragraph break on its own -- the function exists but the one place a paragraph actually gets split never asks it.
acceptance_criteria:
toBlocks treats a line matching opensNumberedParagraph as starting a new
paragraph regardless of indentation or a preceding blank line.
uk-litvinenko-inquiry's 3.75-3.81 render as five separate paragraphs.
pnpm ingest check + corpus check reviewed and accepted across every
report using this numbering convention (at minimum Litvinenko and
Leveson); no false-positive split introduced where a line coincidentally
opens with something matching the pattern (a decimal figure at a line
break, e.g. "3.5 million") -- checked by sampling the corpus diff, not
assumed safe from the regex alone.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.7: a new opt-in pass, numberedParagraphs(),
declared on litvinenko-inquiry, uk-leveson-inquiry, and uk-hillsborough-
panel (the three reports confirmed to use this "N.NN" chapter.paragraph
numbering). toBlocks now reads a genuine two-part numbered opener as a
paragraph break regardless of indentation or a preceding blank line --
opensNumberedParagraph already existed for exactly this shape but was
consulted in only one place (a heading-continuation guard) and never by
toBlocks' own break decision.

Iterated through two real false-positive classes found by reading the
actual corpus diff, not by trusting the regex:
1. Applying it unconditionally moved every report, including ones that
   never use this convention -- Challenger's test-method appendices
   wrap decimal measurements onto their own line ("...compression of
   5.8 to" / "7.0 percent..."), and reading "7.0" as a paragraph opener
   severed a sentence mid-thought. Fixed by making it opt-in.
2. Even scoped to the three reports that do use the convention: a bare
   "N." (Litvinenko's "allocated room\n\n382. Mr Begak...", a room
   number) and a two-part number immediately followed by a quantity
   word ("suggested\n\n1.8 million people...", Leveson) both read as
   paragraph openers. Fixed by requiring both digit groups and adding
   a QUANTITY_WORD_FOLLOWS guard. 4 new tests cover the opt-in gate and
   both guards.

Verified against real data: litvinenko-inquiry +150 paragraphs,
uk-leveson-inquiry +1,818, uk-hillsborough-panel +90 -- all seven other
reports in the corpus completely unaffected (pnpm ingest check green
throughout). Word counts unchanged in all three (content re-segmented,
nothing lost). Sampled dozens of the ~2,058 new splits by hand across
all three reports, all correct, including the specific cases from
uk-litvinenko-inquiry#2 and both false-positive classes found along the
way. Corpus-baseline moves reviewed and accepted (paragraph permalinks
shifted, as they must when previously-merged paragraphs split). Full
local verify.sh green.

title: Make per-chapter footnote identities safe for Leveson
description: Leveson restarts footnote numbering by chapter, while the ingestion pipeline treats a number as report-global. Correct identity and rendering without making marker-linking unsafe.
acceptance_criteria: Every rendered Leveson footnote reference resolves to its own chapter-local definition; no output exceeds deployment asset limits; ingestion checks and rendered-page inspection confirm the result.
notes:
2026-09-11 — Fixed upstream in @rtm/ingest (v0.12.4), verified against real Leveson data, shipped corpus-wide.

Root cause: renderEndnotes/collectNotes/withSidenotes modelled a footnote's identity as its bare number, deduping/looking up by number alone. Any report where two genuinely different notes share a number -- Leveson's deliberate per-chapter restart, or (discovered along the way) OCR misreading a footnote marker's digits so it collides with an unrelated earlier note -- collapsed those notes into one merged definition, and every reference to that number resolved to whichever text won the collapse.

Fix: reference markers are untouched (no change to where/how a [^N] gets written). Definition RESOLUTION is now position-aware: renderEndnotes still merges adjacent same-number entries (exact repeats, page-break tails -- unchanged, same tests pass), but non-adjacent same-number entries stay separate definitions; collectNotes returns all of a number's definitions in document order; withSidenotes resolves each [^N] reference against them positionally (1st reference -> 1st definition, 2nd -> 2nd, ...). New unit + integration tests in @rtm/ingest (243 total passing). Tagged v0.12.4.

Real-data impact was much bigger than the bead described -- this wasn't Leveson-only. Re-ingesting under the fix moved 7 of 10 reports' footnote text (challenger-accident, columbia-accident, jack-smith-vol1, litvinenko-inquiry, uk-leveson-inquiry, us-deepwater-horizon, us-psi-financial-crisis), all verified by direct comparison: body text byte-for-byte identical in every case, only the Notes section changed, growing as merged blobs split back into correct definitions. us-deepwater-horizon was hit hardest -- 1,226 sidenotes, same count before and after, but the rendered page shrank 2.07MB -> 1.78MB because each sidenote now shows only its own text instead of a shared merged blob. All 10 reports pass pnpm ingest verify/check; pnpm corpus check diffs read and accepted (6 reports: footnote-only, zero citable-paragraph impact, confirmed by identical body byte-count; Leveson: real paragraph-id moves too, see below).

Leveson specifically: its own package.json was still pinned to v0.2.1 (never updated since migration), ~10 versions behind. Bumping it to get this fix meant adopting everything else the pipeline gained since too -- footnote recall in particular (8,605 footnotes now found vs the old ~1,680, most previously merged). This DOES move real Leveson paragraph-id citations (23 sections affected, mostly from a few headings losing a spurious 'CHAPTER' prefix that had been concatenating into the section title). Read and accepted deliberately -- see uk-leveson-inquiry's own commit (8fbc371) for the full account. Asset size checked explicitly given the bead's #103 history: full-body.html is 8.9MB, safely under the 25 MiB Cloudflare limit.

Verified via rendered-page inspection (the acceptance criteria's own requirement): of 62 Leveson footnote numbers with more than one resolved occurrence in the final HTML, all 62 now show correctly distinct text -- was effectively 0/63 correct on an earlier, not-yet-fully-baselined check.

Split off, not attempted here: reportsthatmatter-axw (linkInlineMarkers still links some non-footnote numbers -- a few dates, a repeated boilerplate block with a likely-dropped phone-number leading zero -- a pre-existing, separate defect that predates this fix and doesn't dominate the corpus the way the identity bug did, but is visible in spot checks).

Builds on the tooling batch: preflight #230, --all --status #233, incremental reindex and --preflight/--dry-run #237, docs/release-checklist.md #239. description: Make improvement a measured loop, not a bug queue. 1) Dev/held-out split: choose 3-4 reports with reference text as held-out; a pass is developed on the others and must not lower held-out scores (guards against overfitting heuristics to one report). 2) Error clustering: from the scorer's error list, cluster errors automatically (by layout context, page position, block type, neighbouring text shape) and rank clusters by reader impact (words affected, citable ids lost), so the next thing to work on is chosen by data. 3) Release scorecard: the integrator posts the score deltas per report alongside the b78.2 counts in every ingest release PR. 4) Retro: the agent protocol gains a required final-report section, "what slowed us; what would have caught this earlier; one proposed check or tool", and the supervisor rolls these into a running docs/design/lessons.md. 5) Track throughput: defects found by readers vs. checks per release (the b78 catalogue says 0 of ~50 were found by a check). Depends on the scorer.
notes:
Dev/held-out sets come from reports with clean editions, kept as shadow PDF ingests even if served from the clean text (see the 38s notes, 2026-10-02).
Merger retro (2026-10-02): pnpm score should write its headline numbers (per report: boundary P/R/F1, join accuracy on adjudicated breaks, marker P/R, reference error rate) to a committed docs/scores.json. The release scorecard is then a plain diff of that file, and 'does this merge reproduce the PR's numbers?' becomes mechanical. Also from 38s.12: gate scoring on reference/adjudicated.yaml and warn when the reference error rate plus its no-answer share exceeds a ceiling (e.g. 5% + 10%).
Two integrators couldn't check the page-break join accuracy headline: pnpm score must print 'ours wrong / judged' on adjudicated breaks and all-row join accuracy, per set, with the previous recorded value.
2026-10-03: built in site PR #238 (branch loop-38s6): docs/scores.json via pnpm score (dev/held-out from reports/score-sets.yaml, join accuracy all/high/adjudicated, reference-error ceiling warning, previous+delta), pnpm scorecard (quality diff + oracle + golden + scores diff + checklist; reports/verify-last.json base), docs/design/lessons.md, AGENTS.md and scripts/ingest/README.md wired. title: Research: extractor bake-off — pipeline vs. tagged PDF, pdftohtml layout, ML layout extractors, vision LLM
description: Using the alignment scorer and the reference editions, compare extraction approaches on the same 2-3 reports: our pipeline (current passes); tagged-PDF structure where the PDFs carry it; the pdftohtml -xml layout (font size, position) on its own, as in b78.5; one or two ML document-layout extractors (Docling, Marker, or a current equivalent; check licence and local runtime); and a vision LLM per page (cost noted). Report, per approach: scores per metric, speed and cost, and where each wins. Question to answer: should parts of the pipeline (e.g. heading detection, footnote linking, paragraph reflow) be replaced by or combined with another approach (an ensemble: use the layout/ML output as features, or as a vote on ambiguous blocks) rather than adding another heuristic pass? Opus for the analysis.

title: Research: can a vision model produce gold pages? Measure model transcription vs. reference editions and vs. the pipeline
description: Question: can a vision model reading PDF page images produce gold-standard structured text (markdown with headings, paragraph boundaries, block quotes, footnotes and marker links) good enough to score the pipeline against? Method: on 2 reports that have a reference edition (inventory bead), sample about 40 pages each with known hard features (page-break splits, footnotes, quotes, headings, tables), transcribe with Claude (Sonnet and Opus; note the cost per page), and score the transcriptions against the reference with the alignment scorer. Also score the pipeline on the same pages. Report: model accuracy per feature vs. the pipeline's, cost per page, and failure modes (hallucinated text, dropped footnotes). If models are reliable on structure, recommend generating gold pages for every report this way (agents verify, Rufus spot-checks), which changes b78.4 (golden pages) from hand-curated to generated-then-verified. Also consider the model as a referee only for blocks where heuristics disagree.

title: Research: synthetic benchmark — PDFs generated from known markdown with report-like layouts, perfectly labelled
description: Build a synthetic benchmark: generate PDFs from known markdown with typst or LaTeX templates that mimic the layouts that break us: footnotes with flush markers, running heads and folios (arabic and roman), paragraphs and quotations split across page breaks (including a capitalised continuation), block quotations introduced mid-sentence, small-caps headings, rotated side banners, numbered paragraphs with hanging indents, lettered sub-items, two-column pages, tables, gutter shifts and scanned or OCR noise (rasterise and re-OCR some pages). Because the source markdown is known, every page is perfectly labelled. Run @rtm/ingest over it with the relevant passes and score it with the alignment scorer. Uses: a regression suite for each pass (one fixture family per defect class in the b78 catalogue), and a cheap way to try new heuristics without hunting real examples. Measure whether the synthetic scores predict the real-report scores; if they don't, say so. Sonnet, after the scorer exists.
notes: 2026-10-02 from 38s.8: hardest real page-break shapes to synthesise — capitalised run-on onto a recto page whose text block sits at a different left (Saville p395 'Brian' / 'Faulkner'); page ending on a full stop with the paragraph running on, no first-line indent on the next page (PM p1031); block quotation running over a page with no inset on its first line (PM p938-939); citation string continuing a finding (PM p612 '…1992.' / '682515783-5803 (US 88089)'); footnote '(continued...)' between a paragraph and its continuation (PM p1595).

title: Quality harness 4: layout oracle from pdftohtml -xml — headings, markers, paragraph boundaries measured against the pipeline
description:
Layout oracle from `pdftohtml -xml` (plan §3.3). poppler is already installed and `pdftohtml -xml -f N -l N -stdout <pdf>` takes ~0.04 s/page and returns every text line with `top/left/width/height`, a `font` id, and `fontspec size/family/color`. Hillsborough's headings are `#780030` at 18–45pt against black 14pt body text (r19); numbered paragraphs sit at left=80 vs body 122; footnote markers are small raised glyphs. Build a measure-only oracle in @rtm/ingest (`src/oracle.ts`), run by `pnpm ingest verify` per report (cache the XML per PDF sha under `<report-repo>/.cache/`), that compares what the layout says against what the pipeline produced and emits counts into `pnpm quality report` (b78.2 budget file gains these signals once precision is known):

1. Heading oracle: body font = the modal fontspec by character count; a line whose font size ≥ body + 2pt or colour ≠ body colour, alone on its line, is an expected heading. Compare with the pipeline's headings on that page: `headings-missed` (expected, not produced: catalogue I) and `headings-spurious` (produced, body font: catalogue H). Report per report and per page.
2. Marker oracle: glyph runs with font size ≤ body − 3pt whose `top` is above the baseline of the surrounding line and whose text is digits are expected markers; compare with linked `[^N]` on that page: `markers-unlinked` (catalogue F, exact instead of regex) and `markers-spurious` (G).
3. Paragraph-boundary oracle: within the body font, a vertical gap ≥ 1.4 × line pitch, or a first-line indent, starts a paragraph; count expected paragraph starts per page and compare with produced blocks starting on that page: `paragraphs-oversplit` (A/B/C severed sentences including capitalised continuations) and `paragraphs-merged` (fused headings, class I; swallowed captions).
4. Quote oracle: lines whose `left` is indented from the body margin on both sides for ≥ 2 consecutive lines; compare with quote blocks (`quotes-spurious` for class D).

Not a second parser: nothing here changes the output; it only measures. Scanned reports (Challenger, Jack Smith) carry OCR-generated fonts, so run the oracle there too but expect noise; measure precision against the golden pages (b78.4) and report it per report before any oracle signal gets a budget. Deliverable: the module, tests on 3 fixture pages (Hillsborough p.30 headings, a Leveson page with 5+ markers, a Deepwater even page), and a `docs/quality-harness.md` section with the measured precision table.
acceptance_criteria: src/oracle.ts in @rtm/ingest emits headings-missed/spurious, markers-unlinked/spurious, paragraphs-oversplit/merged, quotes-spurious per report; cached XML per PDF sha; precision measured against golden pages and recorded in docs/quality-harness.md before any oracle signal is budgeted.
notes: 2026-10-02 built: ingest PR https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/ingest/pull/37 (src/layout.ts, src/oracle.ts, src/context.ts), site PR https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter/pull/219 (verify runs the oracle, scorer adapter, docs/quality-harness.md oracle section with counts/precision/runtime). title: Quality harness 2: ratchet budgets, quality report in every release PR, retire the 20% severed gate
description:
Second layer (plan §3.1, §4): make the budgets ratchet and make every ingest release carry its quality numbers. Depends on b78.2.

1. Ratchet mechanics: `pnpm quality ratchet` already lowers budgets to current counts; add `--dry-run`, and make `scripts/verify.sh` print a one-line hint when any signal is below its budget by ≥ 10% ("N budgets can be ratcheted: pnpm quality ratchet"). Raising a budget requires a `# why: <bead id>` comment on the changed line; `check` diffs against `git show HEAD:reports/quality-budget.yaml` and fails on an uncommented increase.
2. Release report: `pnpm quality report --diff <git ref>` prints the per-report × per-signal table with the counts at `<ref>` (regenerate `reports/*/full.md` from the pinned ingest at that ref is too slow; instead store `reports/quality-last.json` with the counts at each accepted release, written by `pnpm quality ratchet --record`), the current counts and the deltas, marking regressions. The release/pin-bump PR template (AGENTS.md "Changing the library") requires this table pasted in; `scripts/publish-report.mjs` prints the report's own row before publishing.
3. Retire the two gates the budgets supersede, in @rtm/ingest `fidelity.ts` (separate ingest PR, pin bump): `severedSentenceCheck`'s 20% rate gate becomes informational (its count is now budgeted per report by `severed-into-quote`), and `document has headings` becomes `headings per 100 pages within [3, 60]` reported, not gated (gated by the site budget). Keep `digitDensityCheck`, `losslessCheck`, `retentionCheck`, `structuralChecks` as they are.
4. Docs: AGENTS.md "Know a change's blast radius" gains the third gate (`pnpm quality check`) and the ratchet rule; `scripts/ingest/README.md` and `docs/report-preparation.md` step 3 say "run `pnpm quality report <id>` and read the excerpts" instead of "read the output" alone; a new `docs/quality-harness.md` (short) explains signals, budgets, ratchet, and how to add a signal (fixture from the broken text first).
acceptance_criteria: A raised budget without a '# why:' comment fails check; pnpm quality report --diff shows deltas against the last recorded release; AGENTS.md documents the third gate and the ratchet rule; ingest PR makes severedSentenceCheck and 'document has headings' informational.

title: us-duelfer-report: heading detection still collapses after the banner-splice fix (quote misclassification, no-blank-line headings)
description:
Split off reportsthatmatter-1l4 once the banner-splice fix (ingest PR #22)
proved the heading collapse in Volume I has separate causes -- fixing the
banner did not recover real chapter/section structure (still 1 heading,
"Notes", for a 453-page volume; prerenders to 2 sections).

Two distinct, pre-existing defects found while checking, neither caused by
the banner:

1. Some subsection headings are indented enough that `quoteInset`'s default
   threshold misreads them as block quotations. Example: the body's own
   "Who Made Iraq's Strategic Decisions and Determined WMD Policy" (a
   contents-listed heading) renders as "> Who Made Iraq's Strategic
   Decisions and Determined WMD Policy" in full.md -- a blockquote, not a
   heading. `quoteInset(columns)` is an existing, report-declared pass
   (Litvinenko uses `quoteInset(7)` for the same reason); this report's
   right value hasn't been measured yet.

2. At least one heading has no blank line before its first body paragraph
   in the extracted text, so it never becomes an isolated heading-candidate
   line at all -- it's just glued onto the paragraph. Example: one of the
   two "Key Findings" sections renders as "Key Findings Saddam Husayn so
   dominated the Iraqi Regime that its strategic intent was his alone. He
   wanted to..." as one paragraph (the other "Key Findings" occurrence, in
   the Regime Finance and Procurement chapter, is fine and isolated). This
   may be `listedDivisions()` territory (reads a division's heading from
   the body even with no blank line, per its own contents entry) -- but
   that pass's doc comment describes it as being for a contents *without*
   dot leaders, and this report's contents does have dot leaders, so it
   isn't a drop-in fit without checking.

Not investigated further -- ran out of the hour's budget for the
banner-splice fix session. Whoever picks this up should re-measure heading
count with each of `quoteInset(N)` (try a few values) and `listedDivisions()`
declared, one at a time, against the (now banner-fixed) us-duelfer-report,
same method as reportsthatmatter-1l4: read the diff, don't just watch the
heading count go up.

Research separately: why headings collapse (quoteInset misreads indented subheads; heading with no blank line before body). Candidates to evaluate: larger quoteInset, listedHeadings/contentsOutline, unmarkedHeadings (ingest #19). title: us-lehman-examiner: sentences severed across page breaks (~25 paragraphs)
description:
Ingesting Volume 1 of the Valukas Report (reportsthatmatter-b7z) with @rtm/ingest v0.13.0 (contentsOutline() declared; also tried pageBreakContinuations(), no effect — see below): about 25 paragraphs are a single sentence in the source PDF that the page-break merge splits into two or three separate paragraphs, each getting its own paragraph id. Examples (full.md, current commit):

  "Lehman's failure to disclose the use of an accounting device to significantly and temporarily lower leverage, at the same time that it affirmatively represented those" / [paragraph break] / "\"low\" leverage numbers to investors as positive news, created a misleading portrayal of" / [paragraph break] / "Lehman's true financial health.80 Colorable claims exist against the senior officers..."

  One sentence, three paragraphs, three ids. The middle fragment happens to open on a quotation mark ("low"), which is a real quoted word *inside* the sentence, not a block quotation.

Tried `pageBreakContinuations()` (new in v0.13.0, "rejoins a sentence the page break left in pieces"): re-ingested with it declared and it made no measurable difference — the same ~25 fragments remain unjoined, most likely because its documented behaviour only rejoins a continuation that "opens in lower case" or is "a quotation opening a page after a paragraph that stops mid-sentence... when it opens in lower case, or when it stops mid-sentence too and runs straight into a lower-case paragraph," and explicitly leaves alone anything "opening on a quotation mark." Our fragments mostly continue on an ordinary capitalised word (a new clause of the same sentence, not a new sentence) or, in the case above, on a quotation mark that isn't introducing a block quotation at all — neither shape this pass targets.

Measured on the current committed full.md: of 1,539 paragraph-like blocks, roughly 25 genuine cases end without terminal punctuation and are continued as the next paragraph (a rough heuristic list of the false positives to exclude — headings, table fragments, dashed rules — is in this session's working notes; happy to hand over the exact script).

No existing fidelity check catches this: severedSentenceCheck watches for a paragraph running straight into a *quotation* block, not for a plain paragraph-to-paragraph split with no quotation involved.
acceptance_criteria: A shared pass (or an extension to pageBreakContinuations) rejoins sentences split across a page break into ordinary continuing paragraphs — including the case where the continuation opens on a quotation mark that is part of the original sentence, not a new block quotation — without turning genuine quotations into merged prose elsewhere in the corpus. A fidelity check flags a paragraph that plausibly ends mid-sentence (no terminal punctuation) so this doesn't ship silently again.
notes: 2026-10-02 measured with a heuristic (paragraph before a page marker with no terminal punctuation): Vol 1 21, Vol 3 65. Declared pageBreakContinuations() on the combined report: Vol 3 65 -> 62, Vol 1 21 -> 21, and it moves paragraph ids; not declared. Same finding as before: the pass misses continuations on a capitalised word.

title: ingest: listedDivisions() promotes a contents page's own listing lines as duplicate headings when isContentsPage doesn't recognise it
description: Found while working reportsthatmatter-r19 (Hillsborough headings). Hillsborough's contents page (a Foreword/Part/Chapter/Appendix list, entries laid out title-gap-pagenumber, no dot leaders) is not recognised by isContentsPage, so it is parsed as ordinary body text. listedDivisions() then matches the contents page's own listing lines against the same divisions it is trying to detect from their real body occurrence, promoting each contents-page line as its own (duplicate) heading in addition to the true occurrence later in the document -- e.g. 'Chapter 1: 1981-1989...' appears as a heading once from the contents page itself and once from the real chapter opening. Not adopted for Hillsborough because of this; listedHeadings() + runningFurniture(numbersTrackPages) alone were sufficient there. Needs either teaching isContentsPage to recognise this contents layout, or having listedDivisions skip a page that is mostly its own listing entries.

title: us-duelfer-report: rotated chapter-tab side banner splices into body text (fix in ingest PR #22, unmerged; Duelfer parked)
description:
Volume I of the Duelfer Report (Comprehensive Report of the Special Advisor
to the DCI on Iraq's WMD) sets each chapter's name as a rotated, black
side-banner graphic running the full height of every page ("Regime Strategic
Intent" / "Regime Finance and Procurement"). pdftotext's reading order drops
this banner's text into the line stream at an essentially arbitrary point on
the page -- not consistently at a page edge -- so `runningFurniture()` (which
only strips repeated lines at a page's top/bottom edge) does not catch most
occurrences. `columns()` is also declared (the report is genuinely
two-column in many sections) but does not help with this third, non-column
sidebar zone.

Measured on the current ingest (columns() + runningFurniture() +
listedHeadings(), @rtm/ingest v0.12.21): of 2511 paragraphs, the banner
fragment "Regime Strategic" appears mid-text (not as part of the legitimate
phrase "Regime Strategic Intent") 50 times, and "Regime Finance" (not part of
"Regime Finance and Procurement") 92 times -- 142 total splices across 451
pages, roughly one every three pages. Examples (full.md, current run):

- "was at the point of collapse. His rationale for this Regime Strategic by
  building many palaces the US would be unable to ascertain his whereabouts
  and thus target him." -- the banner is spliced mid-sentence, and the clause
  joining "for this" to "by building" reads as if words are missing around
  the splice.
- "Huwaysh was sacked as Minister of Industry in Regime Strategic ostracized
  for nine years."
- TOC lines are corrupted the same way: "Contents Regime Strategic Key
  Findings -- 1", "Annexes Regime Strategic A. The Quartet...".

Because the chapter contents pages are corrupted by the same defect,
`listedHeadings()` (added to suppress a *different*, worse defect -- see
below) cross-checks candidate headings against a corrupted contents list and
ends up rejecting nearly every real heading too: the volume renders with a
single heading ("Notes") and prerenders to only 2 sections for a 453-page,
168,000-word document.

Without `listedHeadings()`, heading detection instead produces 12 headings,
none of them real chapter/section titles -- e.g. "## Annex C: Regime
Strategic" (truncated by the same banner splice), "## TOTAL" and "## Crude
Oil" (table cells), "### Engineer Azmy Khrisat 1. Mr. Saddam Zaban Hasan"
(a list of names on their own lines), "### O. Box" (a mangled "P.O. Box").

Separately, the report also has a false block quote: the "Acknowledgements"
byline "Acknowledgements (12 September 2004 2330)" renders as a blockquote
(indented, quote-styled) on the report's own first page -- it is not a
quotation. And a stray pilcrow character ("¶") renders as its own bullet
list item at least once (seen just above "Saddam went on a palace and mosque
building extravaganza..."), a fragment of a paragraph-mark glyph in the
source that should have been dropped.

This needs a pass that can identify and strip a non-edge, non-column
furniture zone (the rotated side banner) before line ordering -- geometry-
aware, since the banner sits in a fixed horizontal band down one side of
every page, distinct from both text columns. Per the site's report-
preparation.md instructions, no pass was written for this while ingesting
the report; this bead records the defect with examples and counts for
whoever picks it up (shared pass if the pattern recurs elsewhere in the
corpus, otherwise a pass the report declares in its own ingest.ts).

Report repo: https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/us-duelfer-report
Site branch: duelfer-report
notes:
Also found, same ingest run: the footnote parser produces 2 orphaned
"[^6]:" / "[^11]:" definitions at the back of the document with zero
inline markers anywhere in the body (grep for `\[\^[0-9]*\][^:]` in
full.md matches nothing) -- every footnote reference in this document is
unlinked. Both definitions are garbled, interleaving unrelated sentences
(e.g. "[^6]:" opens "December 1993. and the buyer, Unipack Paris
Company... Figure 30 shows a letter authorizing the Czech Republic
Company..." -- several different captured-document descriptions welded
together). Root cause looks like real annex body prose (a running
description of Figures 21-31, captured-document facsimiles in the Finance
chapter) with an item number like "6." at a line start being misread as a
footnote marker, not a genuine footnote.

Tried declaring `endnotes()` (used successfully by us-911-commission for a
similar back-of-book notes section) to see if it fixed this cleanly: it
does remove the 2 garbled definitions (Footnotes: 0), but it also drops
every heading the pipeline was finding (headings: 0, failing
`pnpm ingest verify`'s heading check outright, worse than the 1-heading
state without it) -- reverted, not used. This confirms the defect needs a
real fix (most likely: whatever misreads "6." as a marker start needs to
stop doing so unless it's actually at a page foot / in a true notes
list), not a different combination of existing passes.

Net effect on verify.sh: `check_contains .../full 'class="sidenote"'`
fails for us-duelfer-report (registry has a `[^` definition but nothing
renders as a sidenote) -- this is the one non-peer failure in an
otherwise-green verify.sh run for this report; recorded here rather than
worked around.
Fixed the banner splice (2026-09-28), per the coordinator's preferred
approach: excluded at extraction rather than pattern-matched after the
fact. `pdfinfo -box` on the Duelfer PDF shows CropBox 612x792 but MediaBox
684x864; `pdftotext -bbox` puts the rotated chapter-tab at x 612-634 --
entirely in the bleed margin beyond the trimmed page. pdftotext's default
extraction reads the whole MediaBox, so the tab reached the line stream.

Added an optional `crop: { x, y, width, height }` on a Volume in @rtm/ingest
(PR https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/ingest/pull/22, v0.14.0, based on
v0.13.0, NOT merged/tagged), passed as pdftotext's own -x/-y/-W/-H ahead of
-layout. Additive: extractPages(path) with no crop is byte-identical to
before, so no other report's output moves (proved via `pnpm ingest check`
after reverting a temporary local pin bump -- see below). Test written
first (tests/extract.test.ts on the pure arg-building function), confirmed
red against origin/main, then green.

us-duelfer-report declares `crop: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 610, height: 828 }`
on its one volume (branch `banner-fix`, DO-NOT-MERGE pinned to the ingest
branch until it's tagged). Before/after on the real report:
- Banner splices (the two chapter-name fragments outside their legitimate
  phrase): 142 -> 2. Both remaining are legitimate: a real subheading
  "Regime Strategic Goals", and one unrelated page-break continuation
  ("...see the Regime Finance and [Procurement chapter]").
- Sentences severed into quotations: 37/2508 (1.5%) -> 14/2265 (0.6%).
- Footnote orphans: unchanged (2 garbled definitions, 0 markers) -- this is
  a separate defect, not caused by the banner; still open.
- Headings: did NOT recover as hoped, even though the chapter contents
  pages are now clean of banner splices. Found two other, unrelated,
  pre-existing causes while checking: (1) quoteInset's default indent
  threshold misreads some indented subsection headings as block quotes,
  e.g. "Who Made Iraq's Strategic Decisions and Determined WMD Policy"
  renders as "> Who Made..."; (2) at least one heading (one of the two
  "Key Findings" occurrences) has no blank line before its first body
  paragraph in the extracted text, so it's never isolated as a heading
  candidate at all. Neither is a banner/crop problem. Not fixed here --
  stopping per instruction rather than scope-creeping into a third fix;
  whoever picks up heading recovery should start from these two findings.

title: us-lehman-examiner: footnote markers not linked in ~15% of body references
description:
Ingesting Volume 1 of the Valukas Report (Lehman Brothers examiner, reportsthatmatter-b7z) with @rtm/ingest v0.12.21 (default passes, no report-declared passes needed otherwise): footnote *definitions* are all correctly extracted (687 defs, `pnpm ingest verify`'s "every footnote reference has a note" check is green), but a large minority of *inline markers* are never linked into `[^N]` form — they stay as bare digits fused to the preceding word or number, exactly like the source PDF's superscript, e.g.:

  - "reported record revenues of nearly $60 billion and record earnings in excess of $4 billion for its fiscal year ending November 30, 2007.2 During January 2008..." (marker 2, unlinked; compare marker 56 two paragraphs later, which IS linked: `...to a cause of action available to the estate."[^56]`)
  - "Lehman used Repo 105 for no articulated business purpose except \"to reduce balance sheet at the quarter‐end.\"24 Rather than sell assets..." (marker 24, unlinked)
  - Worse, inside a financial table rendered as run-on prose: "Reported Net Leverage Leverage Without Repo 105 Q4 2007 $38.6 B71 16.172 17.873" — markers 71/72/73 are fused directly onto the numeric values ($38.6 B + marker 71; 16.1 + marker 72; 17.8 + marker 73), making the printed figure and the footnote number visually indistinguishable in the rendered page.

Measured on the committed full.md (before any report-declared pass): of ~817 total marker occurrences, 122 (108 distinct note numbers, ~15%) are unlinked bare digits; 695 are correctly linked `[^N]`. Not confined to the start of the document — unlinked markers recur throughout (spot-checked up to marker 689 near the end).

No existing fidelity check catches this: "every footnote reference has a note" only checks that a `[^N]` reference has a matching `[^N]:` definition; it says nothing about markers that were never converted to `[^N]` form in the first place, so this whole class of defect is invisible to `pnpm ingest verify`.

This looks like a shared-library gap (footnote inline-marker linking, `linkInlineMarkers`/`linkFlushMarkers` in @rtm/ingest), not something this report's own `ingest.ts` can fix by composing existing passes — flagging for the pipeline rather than writing a new pass myself, per this session's instructions. Needs someone who can reproduce against `us-lehman-examiner`'s archive PDF (pinned sha256 in its ingest.ts) to find why only a subset of markers link.
acceptance_criteria: A shared-pipeline fix (or a named cause ruled report-specific) makes us-lehman-examiner's re-ingested full.md link all 817 footnote marker occurrences to their [^N] definitions, or explains why some are correctly left bare. A new fidelity check (or an extension to the existing footnote check) catches an unlinked-but-defined marker so this class doesn't ship silently again.
notes: 2026-10-02 measured (Valukas Vol 1+3, v0.14.1 default passes): notes with a linked marker in the body: Vol 1 5 of 690, Vol 3 1 of 1094 (the earlier 122-of-817 count included the 690 definitions). Declaring the existing flushFootnoteMarkers() pass: Vol 1 502/690, Vol 3 658/1094. Extending that pass (ingest#25: 4-digit numbers, marker after a year or a closing quote): Vol 1 638/690 (52 unlinked), Vol 3 941/1094 (153 unlinked). Remaining: markers inside tables and after numbers/symbols (e.g. 'B2901 16.12902').

title: pnpm cards: render one card per editorial card:true highlight
description: scripts/cards.mjs only renders a curated card per docs/share-quotes.yaml entry (keyed report/paragraph), plus one plain default per report. It doesn't render a card per editorial/<id>.yaml highlight with card: true, of which there are 61 across the 11 reports. Because of this, pnpm posts (reportsthatmatter-y2t.3) deliberately puts every editorial-origin queue item on the report's plain default card rather than a curated one — even where a share-quotes card happens to exist for that paragraph, since it may show different words. Fix: extend cards.mjs to render a card per (report, paragraph, quote) for every approved editorial highlight with card: true, and update src/lib/posts.ts's resolveCandidate to prefer that specific card for editorial-origin candidates. Natural companion: fold docs/share-quotes.yaml into the editorial files (plan's track A6), which would let cards.mjs read one source instead of two.

title: linkInlineMarkers links a number across a block boundary, fusing the next paragraph into the previous block
description: In @rtm/ingest footnotes.ts linkInlineMarkers matches /([.,;:!?"')])\s+(\d{1,4})(?=\s|$)/ — \s+ spans the blank line between markdown blocks, so a block ending in punctuation followed by a block opening with a known note number is fused: 'VIII. DEFENDANTS HAVE VIOLATED 18 U.S.C. §1962(d)' + '18 U.S.C. § 1962(d) provides...' became one heading with [^18] (us-v-philip-morris). Changing \s+ to [ \t]+ moves 5 other reports: us-deepwater-horizon +209 paragraphs, litvinenko +53, uk-leveson +10, us-psi +8, jack-smith-vol1 +5 (paragraph counts rise because blocks stop fusing) — needs diff review per report before landing.

Corpus moves (paragraph-block diffs read, all genuine un-fusings): deepwater +279 paragraphs, challenger +65 (bead missed it), litvinenko +53, leveson +10, psi +8, jack-smith +5, columbia +3 (bead missed it), philip-morris +3; statute guard moves only jack-smith, deepwater, philip-morris. title: Chilcot Executive Summary: most section headings are set in plain title case and are not recovered as structure
description:
The Executive Summary's own front contents (PDF p.5-6, printed pages 1-2) lists 88 section/subsection entries. With `listedHeadings()` declared (uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts), only 13 come out as `##`/`###` headings in full.md -- the 13 that happen to be set ALL CAPS in the body ("LOOTING IN BASRA", "TRANSITION", etc, all in the post-conflict chapter). The other 75, including top-level sections ("Introduction", "Why Iraq? Why now?", "Weapons of mass destruction", "Key findings"), are set in plain sentence/title case with no numbering, no lettering and no division label ("Part"/"Chapter"/"Section N"), so `isHeadingLine()` never treats the line as heading-shaped in the first place -- `listedHeadings()` only gates candidates isHeadingLine already proposes, it cannot promote a line isHeadingLine rejects. The result: a body line such as "UK policy before 9/11" runs straight into the numbered paragraph after it with no break at all ("UK policy before 9/11 26. Before the attacks on the US..."), and the report reads as one long undifferentiated stream of numbered paragraphs for most of its length.

Examples (all confirmed against `pdftotext -layout`, which shows the heading on its own line with a blank line before it and no distinguishing typography the text layer preserves):
- "Introduction" (page 4) -- fused into the paragraph below.
- "The UK decision to support US military action" (page 6) -- fused: "The UK decision to support US military action 24. President Bush decided...".
- "UK policy before 9/11" (page 6) -- fused: "UK policy before 9/11 26. Before the attacks on the US...".
- "Why Iraq? Why now?" (page 40), "Weapons of mass destruction" (page 69), "Key findings" (page 111) -- all fused the same way.
- 75/88 contents entries in total are missing as headings; run `grep -c "^#" reports/uk-chilcot-inquiry/full.md` (14, including the endnotes "## Notes") against the 88-entry contents list to reproduce the count.

This would need a shared-pipeline change (a pass that, given `listedHeadings`, treats a body line as heading-shaped when it exactly equals a contents entry -- letter for letter -- even without caps or numbering) or a report-owned pass along the lines of Challenger's `isolateDivisionLabels`. Per this session's instructions, no such pass was written; the Executive Summary ships to stage 1 with this limitation recorded in PROCESSING.md.

A second, smaller defect on the same contents page: one entry ("The predicted increase in the threat to the UK as a result of military action in Iraq", ending in the page-number leader "47") had its own leader digit "47" mistaken for an inline footnote marker and rendered as `[^47]`, fusing it with the next entry ("The UK's relationship with the US") into one list item. Source (`pdftotext -f 5 -l 5 -layout`) shows these as two entries on separate lines with a blank line between them; nothing in the source suggests a footnote there.
notes:
Fixed, not yet shipped (per coordinator request mid-session, overriding the original file-a-bead instruction). New opt-in pass unmarkedHeadings() in @rtm/ingest: reportsthatmatter/ingest#19 (branch fix/chilcot-headings, commit 2d823b5) -- a line with no heading shape of its own still opens a heading when it matches a contents entry letter for letter and the preceding line on the same page ends cleanly (guards against a heading opening on a sentence continued from the page before -- found one real case, 'reconstruction.' on p.85, which coincides with a genuine heading elsewhere). Report repo: reportsthatmatter/uk-chilcot-inquiry#1, pinned to the ingest commit pending the real v0.13.0 tag. Recovers 69/88 contents-listed headings (up from 13/88), zero false positives verified against the whole document. Checked directly against the corpus: us-v-philip-morris (contentsOutline) and challenger-accident (listedHeadings) both byte-identical when rebuilt against this ingest commit -- no other report moves. Remaining 19/88: page-opening headings (no prior line on that page to check), two-line-wrapped titles, and the one contents-entry-fused-with-footnote-marker case -- all recorded in PROCESSING.md. Not merged/tagged/deployed -- needs: ingest PR merged + tagged v0.13.0, report repo repinned to the tag, site's own ingest pin bumped, re-ingest + re-verify (site PR #181).
2026-10-02: last 19 headings recovered with a new opt-in pass recoverListedHeadings() (ingest PR #30, branch feat/chilcot-lessons-headings, fa795b3), declared in uk-chilcot-inquiry/ingest.ts (report PR #2, branch fix/lessons-headings, pinned to that commit pending a tag). Cases: page-top heading (guarded so 'reconstruction.' is still refused), heading after a footnote-marker line end, two-line titles (wrapped contents entries listed whole), caps title ending in a number (read as page number), single-dot contents leader ('Iraq . 47') which also fixes the fused contents entry. Headings 68 to 90 (all 88 contents entries); numbered paragraphs 1-911 intact; citable ids 956 to 953 (3 bare lines Transition/Preparation for withdrawal/Key findings became headings); 19 numbered-paragraph ids rename (heading words dropped from slug) and 385 ids move section. Editorial updated in site PR #205 (3 ids, 2 guide entries retargeted, 3 Lessons guide entries added); pnpm editorial clean against the rebuilt report. Integrator: release ingest, bump site pin, repin report, re-ingest, copy full.md/PROCESSING.md to reports/uk-chilcot-inquiry/, accept ingest baseline + corpus entry, reseed highlights (changed highlight id). Separate finding: 280/283 notes in this report have no linked marker (b94).
