title: Roll out pageBreakContinuations to the other reports (page-break splits)
description: pageBreakContinuations (ingest#15) is opt-in; only jack-smith-vol1 declares it. pageBreakSplits count (paragraph+quote+skewQuote) per report, 2026-09-28: uk-leveson-inquiry 36 (35 quote, 1 skew), us-v-philip-morris 16 (quote), challenger-accident 9 (5 quote, 4 skew; 7 are OCR noise), us-911-commission 5 (3 quote, 2 skew, the skews are endnote lists), columbia-accident 4, uk-hillsborough-panel 4, uk-saville-inquiry 2, litvinenko/psi/deepwater 0, jack-smith 8→0. Not safe to adopt blindly. 11 of Leveson's 36 are a real quotation whose first half, on the previous page, was read as prose (the paragraph opens with a quotation mark): the right fix joins the prose INTO the quote, not the other way. Several Philip Morris cases are genuine block quotations run into the sentence ('RJR stated that / > if you broadly define…'). Per report: declare the pass, read every move with pnpm ingest check and corpus check, and consider extending the pass for the quote-tail case first. Hillsborough, Columbia and Saville cases looked like genuine continuations on a skim.
acceptance_criteria: Each report with splits either declares the pass, with its moves read and accepted, or records why not; per-report before/after counts noted.
notes:
2026-10-02 (hcs session): declared pageBreakContinuations in hillsborough (4 moves), columbia (3, not 4: pageBreakSplits shows 3 quote + 27 capitalised), saville (2). Read every move: all genuine continuations (Hillsborough paras 60, 99, 120, 136 of chapters 4/9/11; Columbia 'The following section recounts in / chronological order', F6.3-3, F10.4-3; Saville Faulkner 'It was not / generally appreciated', MacLellan 'no / military commander'). title: [epic] Systematic test harness for report processing: catch rendering/structure defects before readers do
description:
Rufus, 2026-09-27, on reportsthatmatter-ca3 (GH jack-smith-report#1): why aren't these being caught? Readers keep finding defects the pipeline should detect itself: paragraphs severed at page breaks, body text set as block quotations, footnote text in the body, headings made from body text, lost paragraph ids, truncated headings. Each is fixed one by one as a bug bead, with nothing that would catch the class next time.

Goal: a systematic harness that measures text/structure quality across the whole corpus on every ingest change, so regressions and unfixed classes are visible without a human reading pages.

Not for this session. Plan it properly. First step (child bead): build a catalogue of examples of what we have been missing, so we know the shape of the problem. Then search for systematic solutions (e.g. corpus-wide invariant checks / lint rules with counts per report, golden-page fixtures against the PDF, differential checks between pdftotext and other extractors, sampled LLM or human review, a 'defect budget' per report in verify).
acceptance_criteria: A written plan (docs/design/...) agreed with Rufus, derived from the examples catalogue, with child beads for implementation.
notes: 2026-10-02: plan written (docs/design/2026-10-02-quality-harness-plan.md, PR on branch design/quality-harness) from the catalogue (b78.1). Child beads b78.2 (lint + budgets, start here), b78.3 (ratchet + release report), b78.4 (golden pages), b78.5 (pdftohtml -xml oracle), b78.6 (sampled LLM review), b78.7 (reader intake). Decisions for Rufus in plan §7.

comments.author: Rufus Pollock
comments.text:
Added one corpus-wide invariant check as part of fixing reportsthatmatter-4qw (Chilcot's 892 numbered paragraphs rendering as an ordered list with no id): paragraph-ids-per-1,000-words, in src/lib/density.ts (paragraphDensityCheck), wired into `pnpm corpus check` (scripts/corpus.mjs) so it runs unconditionally on every report, not just on a baseline diff — the Chilcot defect shipped for a full release without moving any baseline, since a baseline records whatever shipped, not whether it was right.

Threshold MIN_PARAGRAPH_IDS_PER_1000_WORDS = 4, calibrated the same way ingest's digitDensityCheck is: measured across the 13-report corpus (2026-09-28), the legitimate floor is jack-smith-vol1 at 6.73/1000; pre-fix Chilcot measured 1.07/1000; post-fix Chilcot measures 15.52/1000. Threshold sits well below the legitimate floor and well above the broken value. Test: tests/density.test.ts — fails on the pre-fix numbers, passes on the fix and on every other current report.

This is exactly the kind of "corpus-wide invariant check with counts per report" this epic is scoping — a small, narrow instance of it. Worth folding into whatever systematic harness comes out of b78.1's catalogue rather than treated as separate.

title: Catalogue the defects readers and agents have found that the pipeline missed
description: First step of reportsthatmatter-b78. Go through closed and open bug beads (labels ingestion, report ids), GitHub issues on the report repos, and handoff notes; record each missed defect as an example: report, URL/paragraph id, defect class (page-break split, false block quote, footnote-in-body, heading from body text, missing id, truncated heading, ...), how it was found (reader, agent writing an intro, verify), and whether any existing check could have caught it. Output: docs/design/<date>-quality-harness/examples.md with a tally by class. Do not design the solution here.
acceptance_criteria: examples.md exists with at least every defect class from the existing bug beads, each with 1+ concrete example and a count; tally by class and by how-found.
notes:
missing id: non-ASCII paragraph ids (U+02BC etc.) absent from meta.paragraphToSection because ingest's paragraphIndex()/extractPassages() read ids back out of HTML with /[a-z0-9-]+/ while paragraphId() itself allows any \p{L}\p{N} — columbia-accident 176, uk-leveson-inquiry 4, us-911-commission 2, us-v-philip-morris 2, jack-smith-vol1 1 (reportsthatmatter-4k6). Found by an agent writing the Columbia introduction noticing it had to avoid paragraphs; no check (verify.sh, ingest check, corpus check) caught it, because corpus check fingerprints exactly the ids these same functions produce — a shared blind spot in the producer and the checker.
- page-break split hidden behind 2+ page markers / continuation set as a block quote at a skewed page top: jack-smith-vol1 the-results-of-the-investigation ('claims of election'/'fraud-and…'). Found by a reader (Rufus, GH jack-smith-report#1). Not caught: severedSentenceCheck looks only at the next block, and only at quotes. New measure pageBreakSplits (ingest#15) catches it (corpus: 84 splits before).
deepwater (2026-09-28): book gutter — even pages 4-5 cols further in turned 816 paragraphs into blockquotes, no check caught it (a 'quote share by page parity' or 'quote share of body' check would); chapter openers with title lines and no blank folded into first paragraph (no check on headings vs contents); page-foot photo credit swallowing the cross-page continuation.
Chilcot Executive Summary (reportsthatmatter-rcz, defect bead reportsthatmatter-ixe): defect class "heading fused into body text" (inverse of the usual "body text mistaken for heading"). 75 of 88 contents-listed section/subsection headings are plain title case with no caps/numbering/division-label signal, so isHeadingLine() never proposes them as heading candidates and listedHeadings() has nothing to gate -- they run straight into the paragraph after them, e.g. "UK policy before 9/11 26. Before the attacks on the US on 11 September 2001 (9/11), the UK was pursuing...". Found by: agent doing the stage-1 ingest, reading full.md against the source contents page. No existing check catches it -- `pnpm ingest verify`'s only heading check is "document has headings" (count > 0), which 14 recovered headings satisfies. Second smaller example, same report: a contents entry's own page-number leader digit ("47") was mistaken for an inline footnote marker and rendered as `[^47]`, fusing two separate contents entries into one list item -- defect class "spurious footnote marker from unrelated digit".
- (9ek, us-v-philip-morris) Paragraphs opening 'N. ' render as <ol><li> with no id: 4,088 findings were uncitable and every gate passed. A check could count top-level <ol> not inside a blockquote.
- (9ek) Running-furniture detection masks digits, so record citations recurring at page edges ('1350 at 1346 (US 63531).') were deleted: ~270 lines lost, not caught because retention is 96.7% anyway.
- (9ek) Per-page double-spacing detection missed 268 quote-heavy pages -> one paragraph per line. A check could flag runs of short paragraphs that do not end in sentence punctuation.
- (72f/yun) linkInlineMarkers spans blank lines, fusing a paragraph into the heading above as a 'note'. A check could flag headings containing [^N] followed by more than a few words.
tk8 (Columbia): (1) running-furniture stripped repeated-with-digits lines that were not furniture ('CHAPTER 1'…'CHAPTER 11', 'ENDNOTES FOR CHAPTER n'), dropping every chapter heading and taking the chapter number as the printed page — no check flags a printed page sequence that jumps backwards (…19, 1, 22… / …47, 3, 50…). (2) Also lost real text: citation tails like '11, 2001.' stripped as footers in 9/11/Philip Morris/Hillsborough — word-retention % didn't notice. (3) Speaker labels moved across a column split and first letters eaten ('light:', 'MACS:') — words-not-in-source missed it because 'light' is a word. (4) Sidebar/figure caps lines as h2 sections (107 in Columbia), so body text filed under the wrong section — no check compares headings to the report's own contents list. (5) Missing numbered sections the contents lists (1.3, 6.3…) — same gap. (6) Literal '#' paragraph rendered as h1.
us-lehman-examiner (Valukas Report Vol 1, reportsthatmatter-b7z): two defect classes found ingesting with @rtm/ingest v0.12.21, neither caught by pnpm ingest verify — filed as reportsthatmatter-0bf (footnote markers) and noted here (master table of contents), examples below.

1. footnote-in-body / unlinked markers (reportsthatmatter-0bf): 122/817 (~15%) inline footnote markers stay bare digits (e.g. "...ending November 30, 2007.2 During January 2008") instead of linking to [^N], including markers fused into numeric table values ("$38.6 B71 16.172" — marker glued onto the printed figure itself). Found by: agent reading rendered output during report-preparation (report-preparation.md step 3's "read the output, not just the counts"). No check could have caught it: "every footnote reference has a note" only checks [^N] vs [^N]: pairing, not whether a marker was ever converted to [^N] form.

2. front-matter table of contents rendered as body content: Volume 1's PDF opens with the whole 9-volume/2,200-page report's master contents (~1,900 of ~4,000 full.md lines) before Volume 1's own text begins. Entries are dot-leader label+page fused with no space ("Barclays....................703"); the render step splits them into readable bullets ("- (f) Barclays — 703"), which is good for a reader, but the source-word tokenizer that losslessCheck uses never adds the split-off trailing-digit token to its source vocabulary (it only does this for footnote-marker stems), so a document with a long enough dot-leader contents section can fail losslessCheck's <0.1%-foreign-words threshold purely from this (us-lehman-examiner: 152/67598 ≈0.22%) even though nothing was actually invented. Separately, some contents entries lose their own numbers ("## VOLUME" heading with no volume number) and a roman-numeral page marker ("xi") leaks into the bullet list as its own line. Likely addressed by the in-flight contentsOutline pass (ingest PR #18, targeted v0.13.0) rather than needing a new bead — watching for that tag before deciding whether to file one.
us-duelfer-report (Duelfer Report Vol I, stage-1 ingest, 2026-09-28): a new
defect class not yet in the tally -- a rotated, full-page-height side-banner
graphic (the chapter-name tab) whose text is inserted mid-line at an
arbitrary point in the reading order, not at a page edge, so the existing
`runningFurniture()` (edge-only) pass cannot catch it. 142 splices counted
across 451 pages (grep for the two chapter-name fragments minus their
legitimate in-prose uses). Example: "was at the point of collapse. His
rationale for this Regime Strategic by building many palaces the US would be
unable to ascertain his whereabouts..." Found by: agent doing the ingest,
reading full.md and the rendered page (verify.sh's word-count and
severed-quotation checks both passed). Also collapsed heading detection to 1
heading for a 453-page report once `listedHeadings()` was added to suppress
a worse defect (garbage headings from table cells/name lists), because the
contents pages are corrupted by the same banner splice and no longer
text-match the body. Separately: a "false block quote" example -- the byline
"Acknowledgements (12 September 2004 2330)" renders as a blockquote on the
report's own front page, and a stray pilcrow character ("¶") renders as
its own bullet list item. Full writeup: reportsthatmatter-1l4.
challenger-accident (headings, 2026-09-28, reportsthatmatter-c1y): a report whose contents page lists only its ~10 top-level chapters, not subsections, so listedHeadings()/contentsOutline()/unlistedHeadingsMinor() all fail here (tested: listedHeadings dropped 221 headings to 12, taking real chapters like SOLID ROCKET MOTORS and EXTERNAL TANK with it) -- none of the contents-driven heading passes can recover structure when the source's own contents is coarser than its actual sectioning. ~200 of Challenger's 244 headings were figure/table captions, flowchart box labels (repeated 'MORTON THIOKOL', 'FIGURE'), and chronology-line fragments ('Fletcher, the Solid Rocket Motor Source Evaluation Board (SEB)', one sentence split at a line wrap). Fixed with a report-local denylist BodyPass (dropCaptionHeadings) rather than a shared pass, since the set is one-document-specific. Found by: agent reading the bead's own examples plus a full heading-list read of the rendered report; verify.sh's heading-count check does not fail on wrong headings, only zero headings.
challenger-accident (footnote-as-body, 2026-09-28, reportsthatmatter-48o): 6 paragraphs are footnote-block text left in the body because their note numbers are OCR-garbled ('101...102' is clean and still misses; '107...lo8...* O Q' has garbled numbers) so footnoteBlock's sequential-number detector doesn't recognise the block as notes. Not fixed this session -- recorded as unfixable in the bead pending a footnote-block detector tolerant of a broken number sequence. Same shape as g1f but g1f's fixes (run-over blocks, short pages) don't cover a mid-sequence garbled number.
challenger-accident (severed sentence, 2026-09-28, reportsthatmatter-m2y): a sub-shape pageBreakContinuations() (ca3) does not cover -- a block quotation stops mid-sentence at a page break and the continuation on the far side is read as plain paragraphs, not as a resumed quotation, so the merge condition (paragraph-into-quotation) never triggers. Adopting the pass fixed a parallel plain-paragraph instance of the same underlying sentence (Issue 2, Finding 2) but not the quotation instance in the Conclusions. Found by: agent reading the rendered Conclusions page against the bead.
footnote-in-body, run-over spanning several ordinary paragraphs (not one
double-spaced run): us-psi-financial-crisis, 17 body paragraphs across ~10
pages (e.g. 'D. Ratings Deficiencies' page-neighbour paragraphs, the "BSAM
mark recap" note). Found by an agent reading the rendered page against the
bead's own regex measurement (SCO-/GS MBS-E/Hearing Exhibit/etc. after
stripping [^N]); no check (verify.sh, ingest check, corpus check) catches a
footnote printed as body text at all -- word/paragraph counts don't
distinguish where the words landed. (reportsthatmatter-626)

heading deleted as page furniture: uk-hillsborough-panel, all 12 chapter and
3 part openings, because the same title also recurs verbatim as a running
header on every later page of that chapter and furnitureKey() (digits
blanked) can't tell a chapter banner from a real running header. Found by
reading the rendered contents/structure against the source PDF (prior
session, reportsthatmatter-r19); no check flags a heading count that drops
to near zero, and 'document has headings' only checks the count is
non-zero, not that the count is plausible for the page count.
(reportsthatmatter-r19, fixed by ingest's runningFurniture(numbersTrackPages))
us-911-commission (2026-09-28): a body-less chapter banner ("THE SYSTEM WAS BLINKING RED") folded backward into the end of the previous chapter's last numbered section, and every numbered section sat flush with its chapter (no nesting) — reportsthatmatter-u88. Found by a reader/agent reading the rendered contents and section pages, not by any check: word-count and paragraph-count fidelity checks are blind to which section a paragraph landed in, only that it landed somewhere.
us-911-commission (2026-09-28): once endnotes() (v0.12.21) stopped the printed "Notes" appendix being misread as page-foot footnote blocks, its ~34,000 words of raw text had nowhere else to go and sat in the body as plain paragraphs, run-together block quotes, and two misdetected ### headings ("Government's Evidentiary Proffer…") — reportsthatmatter-60p. No check caught it: word-retention counted the text as present (it was, just malformed), and nothing checks the ratio of quote-blocks to paragraphs, which would have flagged 402 quotes as an outlier for prose this size.
us-lehman-examiner, third defect class (reportsthatmatter-1xr): severed sentence across a page break, plain paragraph-to-paragraph (no quotation involved) — "Lehman's failure to disclose the use of an accounting device to significantly and temporarily lower leverage, at the same time that it affirmatively represented those" / "\"low\" leverage numbers to investors as positive news, created a misleading portrayal of" / "Lehman's true financial health.80 Colorable claims exist..." — one sentence, three paragraphs, three ids. ~25 instances. Found by: agent reading the rendered /full page (report-preparation.md's "look at rendered pages"). Not caught by severedSentenceCheck, which only watches a paragraph running into a *quotation* block — this is paragraph-to-paragraph, no quotation. Tried the new (v0.13.0) pageBreakContinuations() pass; measured no change, since its documented trigger (continuation "opens in lower case") doesn't match our fragments, which mostly continue on a capitalised clause or on a quotation mark that is itself part of the sentence rather than introducing a block quote.

Also correcting my earlier note on this bead about the master-table-of-contents defect (reportsthatmatter-b7z / see ingest.ts there): tested the new contentsOutline() pass against it directly — it does NOT fix the losslessCheck failure (the dot-leader style there has no spaces between the leader dots at all, unlike the spaced-leader shape contentsOutline reads), so that one still needed a report-level scoping fix (ingesting only the volume's own pages, not the whole-work's master contents), not a pipeline pass. contentsOutline() *did* turn out to be a big win for a different reason: on the volume's own (much shorter, spaced-out) local contents page it recovers ~55 real subsection headings in the body ("Business and Risk Management") that were previously invisible flat prose — worth knowing as a positive data point for the epic, not just the misses.
missing id (wholesale): uk-chilcot-inquiry — 892 numbered paragraphs ('13. …' at the margin) rendered as Markdown ordered-list items with no id; 60 of ~950 paragraphs citable (reportsthatmatter-4qw). Found by an agent writing the Chilcot intro; no check caught it (an 'ids per 1,000 words' or 'body text in id-less <li>' check would).

title: challenger-accident: Conclusions' key sentence severed across p. 4-5 (block quotation + orphan paragraphs)
description: In the Conclusions (printed pp. 4-5), the indented passage after 'In other areas, the Committee reached somewhat different conclusions than the Rogers Commission:' renders as a block quotation that stops mid-sentence ('...poor technical decision-making over a period of several years by top NASA'), and the rest continues as separate id'd paragraphs 'and contractor personnel, who failed to act decisively to solve the increasingly serious anomalies in the Solid' and 'Rocket Booster joints.' (ids contractor-personnel-who-failed-act, rocket-booster-joints). Same pattern at 'there-no-sense-urgency-their' ('...Rather,') / 'nasa-chose-continue-fly-flawed'. A stray "conclusion.'" footnote mark sits in the quote. This is the report's central departure from the Rogers Commission and cannot be quoted cleanly; the introduction (g0w.7.6) paraphrases it instead. Also: the compilation's '(9) only by the manufacturer...' paragraph (9-only-manufacturer-which-can) is the severed end of Issue 2 finding 2.
notes:
This is the ca3 page-break-continuation class for at least 2 of its 3 instances: 'over a period of several years by top NASA' (page 4) / 'and contractor personnel, who failed...' (page 5) is a textbook page-break split (no terminal punctuation, lower-case continuation, exactly one %%page%% marker between); the compilation's '(9) only by the manufacturer...' is the same shape. Adopted @rtm/ingest's pageBreakContinuations() (reportsthatmatter-ca3, merged in v0.13.0) in ingest.ts. Result: fixes the Issue 2/Finding 2 instance of the '...recipes known / only by the manufacturer...' sentence (now one paragraph) but NOT the Conclusions block quotation -- that one doesn't resume as a quotation on the far side of the page break (it resumes as plain paragraphs), which is outside the shape pageBreakContinuations currently merges (paragraph-into-quotation, not quotation-into-paragraph), so it's still 3 separate blocks. Also NOT a page-break case: 'There was no sense of urgency...Rather,' / 'NASA chose to continue to fly...' splits mid-page (no %%page%% marker between them at all) -- a different, still-unexplained mid-paragraph blank-line artifact inside the same block quote, left as-is. Net: Challenger should keep pageBreakContinuations() (real improvement, already declared), but the Conclusions' central departure from the Rogers Commission remains unquotable cleanly -- the introduction (g0w.7.6) is right to paraphrase it rather than wait for this. Filing a narrower gap in pageBreakContinuations (quotation resuming as prose after a mid-sentence page break) is a decision for whoever owns reportsthatmatter-ca3/kb4, not done here.
Release 2 (ingest v0.14.0, PR challenger-accident#1): partially fixed. pageBreakContinuations was adopted for this report (also referenced by that PR) and rejoins many page-break-split paragraphs elsewhere, but the specific defect described here is unchanged after re-ingest: the Conclusions block quotation still stops mid-sentence at '...top NASA' (full.md line ~175) with the orphaned continuation still separate ('and contractor personnel...Solid' / 'Rocket Booster joints.', full.md lines 179/181), and the compilation's '(9) only by the manufacturer...' stray paragraph is also still separate (full.md line 259). Left open.
2026-10-02: fixed for the Conclusions quotation and the 'Rather,' / 'NASA chose to continue' mid-paragraph break (challenger-accident PR #2, ingest PR #28). Root cause was not pageBreakContinuations: printed p.5 is shifted 3 columns right (body at indent 3, document margin 0) so every line opened a paragraph, and lines merged only where the next began in lower case; breaks fell exactly before capitalised lines ('Rocket Booster joints.', 'NASA chose', 'Space Shuttle Main Engine'). Two new opt-in passes: shiftedPages() (page margin from the page's own body only when commonest indent == least indent, 2-6 columns in, >=15 lines; geometry('per-page') was the first attempt and turned 160 real testimony quotations into prose) and quoteRunOn() (lower-case page-top paragraph joins a quotation stopping mid-sentence). Conclusions quotation now ends '...top NASA and contractor personnel, who failed to act decisively to solve the increasingly serious anomalies in the Solid Rocket Booster joints.'. Editorial yaml re-pointed in site PR #202. Still there: the stray "conclusion.'" mark (OCR'd note 1) inside the quote; the (9) 'only by the manufacturer' sentence was already fixed by v0.14.0.
2026-10-02 (integrator): merged. ingest v0.15.0 tagged; report repo PR merged with pin bumped to v0.15.0 and re-ingested under it; site PRs merged (integration PR #207); corpus and ingest baselines accepted after reading each diff. NOT yet live: wrangler auth expired (see the needs-user bead), so deploy, publish and D1 seed are pending. Close once live.

title: us-deepwater-horizon: chapter headings not detected; figure captions became sections
description: The report's sections are figure captions and map labels ('SANTA BARBARA OIL SPILL', 'AUGER TENSION-LEG PLATFORM', 'DEVELOPMENT & PRODUCTION PLAN ... FIRST OIL / GAS PRODUCTION', 'SHELLFISH CORALS', 'MS AL LA GA', 'MACONDO WELL', 'Jackson Eaton Scott McKee') plus Chapter 9's 'The Need for...' subheads (some truncated: '...to Improve Spill', '...Based on Natural'). None of the ten chapter headings ('Chapter One ...' to 'Chapter Ten ...') or the Foreword is a section; they are merged into the first paragraph of each chapter. The Foreword and Chapters 1-2 all fall under 'Front matter', and paragraphs there carry no page number (p.?). The introduction (reportsthatmatter-g0w.7.8) overrides reading-guide titles to work round this. Similar to reportsthatmatter-h0l (Wall Street).
notes: 2026-09-28: New opt-in passes listedDivisions() (divisions read from a gap-set contents, matched over wrapped chapter-opener lines, 'Chapter Three' = 'Chapter 3') and wrappedHeadings() (ingest#16), plus allCapsHeadings(false) to drop caption headings. Headings now: Foreword, Part I-III, Chapter One-Ten, Chapter 9 subheads (no longer truncated), Endnotes, Appendix A-F, Index. title: columbia-accident (and others): paragraph ids with non-ASCII characters (ʼ) missing from paragraphToSection, so ?p= links to them fail
description:
@rtm/ingest dist/sections.js paragraphIndex() matches ids with /\bid="([a-z0-9-]+)"/, but slugs keep the report's U+02BC apostrophe (e.g. management-decisions-made-during-columbiaʼs, boardʼs-view-nasaʼs-organizational-culture). Those paragraphs have no entry in meta.paragraphToSection: pnpm paragraphs lists them under section 'undefined', ?p= returns 200 without redirecting to the paragraph, and they cannot be cited or highlighted in context. Counts of non-ASCII

ids in prerendered full-body.html: columbia-accident 176, uk-leveson-inquiry 4, us-911-commission 2, us-v-philip-morris 2, jack-smith-vol1 1. Fix either the slugger (fold ʼ and other non-ASCII to ASCII) or the idPattern; the former changes ids, so check the corpus blast radius and existing marks. Found while writing the Columbia introduction (reportsthatmatter-g0w.7.7), which avoided these paragraphs.
notes:
Fixed in @rtm/ingest: paragraphIndex() (sections.ts) and extractPassages()'s CITABLE_UNIT (passages.ts) read ids back out of rendered HTML with /[a-z0-9-]+/, but paragraphId() (markdown.ts) already allowed any \p{L}\p{N} character — so a non-ASCII opening word produced an id neither lookup could see. Widened both regexes to a shared PARAGRAPH_ID_CHARS = [\p{L}\p{N}-]+ (u flag) exported from markdown.ts, so id-consumers can't drift from the id-producer again. Did not touch slugify() or paragraphId() — no paragraph id changes shape. Ingest PR (not merged): https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/ingest/pull/14 Branch: fix/non-ascii-paragraph-ids Added failing-first tests (tests/markdown.test.ts, tests/passages.test.ts) reproducing the Columbia example; confirmed both fail against the pre-fix pattern and pass with the fix. pnpm test: 388/388. pnpm typecheck, pnpm check-dist both clean. Measured by pointing the site worktree (rtm-nonascii-ids) at this ingest worktree via `pnpm add @rtm/ingest@link:../ingest-nonascii-ids`, running `pnpm prerender` before/after, then reverting the link (never committed — site package.json/pnpm-lock.yaml stay on the released v0.12.21 pin). Non-ASCII

ids missing from meta.paragraphToSection, before -> after: columbia-accident 176 -> 0 uk-leveson-inquiry 4 -> 0 us-911-commission 2 -> 0 us-v-philip-morris 2 -> 0 jack-smith-vol1 1 -> 0 (matches this bead's own counts exactly.) Proved no existing id changed: full-body.html is byte-identical before/after for all 11 reports (diff -q clean), and a full paragraphToSection diff per report shows 0 changed existing entries anywhere — only new keys added (the previously-invisible non-ASCII ones). `pnpm corpus check` reports these 5 reports as "moved" (citable-paragraph count increased per section), which is `pnpm corpus accept`'s job once the integrator does the real pin bump — it is new ids appearing, not existing ones moving; do not accept until the real re-ingest, and read the diff again then to confirm the same shape. Grepped for the same ASCII-only id assumption elsewhere and found nothing else to fix: scripts/paragraphs.mjs already uses [^"]+; src/templates/report.ts and scripts/cards.mjs treat the id as an opaque string (regex-escaped, not character-class-restricted); assets/share.js and assets/highlight.js read `.id` as a DOM property; the ?p=/?h= redirect in src/index.ts does a plain object-key lookup on meta.paragraphToSection with encodeURIComponent, no pattern. scripts/verify.sh and three site test files (head.test.ts, social-proof-routes.test.ts, routes.test.ts) do use /[a-z0-9-]+/ to pick an *arbitrary* paragraph id for smoke-testing purposes unrelated to this defect (they just skip past a non-ASCII id to the next ASCII one) — left as is, not a functional bug, and not in the bead's named list of files. No site-repo code change was needed — the site's own src/lib/* has no paragraph-id-reading logic of its own; it all comes from @rtm/ingest via prerender.mjs (renderArtifacts) and index-search.mjs (extractPassages). So no site PR opened; the site worktree (rtm-nonascii-ids) is back on a clean fix/non-ascii-paragraph-ids branch identical to origin/main, no commits. For the integrator: bump @rtm/ingest past this PR, run `pnpm ingest check` (should be clean — no markdown changed), `pnpm corpus check` (will show exactly the 5 reports above as moved — read the diff, confirm only additions as shown here, then `pnpm corpus accept`), re-run `pnpm prerender` and `pnpm index-search` so the search table picks up the newly-citable passages, then verify a couple of the added ids resolve via ?p= on columbia-accident and jack-smith-vol1.

title: uk-leveson-inquiry: chapter headings attached to the wrong body text
description:
In uk-leveson-inquiry's rendered meta.json/sections, several chapter headings are attached to the wrong paragraph, so the section they head is not what the heading says.

Clearest case: the heading "Chapter 7: Conclusions and recommendations for future regulation" (the real Part K chapter, in which Leveson sets out and defends his recommended regulatory model) is attached at two places that are NOT that chapter — the very start of Part A (slug chapter-7-conclusions-and-recommendations-for-future-regulation, page ~3, which actually opens Part A's real content) and its own front-matter TOC line. Meanwhile the chapter's real content — numbered paragraphs 7.1-7.12, e.g. "This legislative proposal does no more than ensure an appropriate degree of independence... This is not, and cannot be characterised as, regulation of the press" — sits ungrouped under the unrelated heading '"GUARANTEE OF MEDIA FREEDOM' (slug guarantee-of-media-freedom-2, p.1781), which is itself a different chapter's (mislabeled?) heading.

Second case: "PART H" (slug part-h, p.999) is followed by no further heading until p.1122, so it silently swallows several real chapters — Part H's own Chapters 1-7 (Introduction through Summary of recommendations, pp.999-1111) AND the start of Part I (press and politicians) — into one ~120-page section.

Likely cause: the heading-detection pass matches on heading TEXT appearing in large font (both the real chapter opening and, separately, that same text rendered large in a volume's front-matter TOC), but doesn't reliably anchor to the correct occurrence's body position — similar in kind to the truncated-heading class of bug already tracked (reportsthatmatter-b5x), but here the heading is complete and simply mis-positioned rather than cut off.

Impact: paragraph ids and citations are unaffected and resolve correctly (verified via pnpm paragraphs/pnpm editorial) — only the section/contents-page grouping and headings are wrong. Worked around in editorial/uk-leveson-inquiry.yaml's reading guide with title overrides on the two affected reading-guide entries (guarantee-of-media-freedom-2 -> "Chapter 7: Conclusions and recommendations for future regulation"; chapter-the-press-and-the-police-conclusions-and-recommendations and part-l-summary-of-recommendations also overridden for their shouted all-caps headings, a separate, minor issue). The contents page itself still shows the misattached headings uncorrected, since title overrides only apply within the editorial reading guide.

Fix belongs in the ingest pipeline (@rtm/ingest heading-detection pass), not the editorial file, per AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: uk-leveson-inquiry re-ingested with @rtm/ingest heading-detection fix; chapter-7-conclusions-and-recommendations-for-future-regulation's section boundary covers paragraphs 7.1-7.12 (the actual Chapter 7 content) rather than Part A's opening; PART H is split into its real constituent chapters; pnpm corpus check accepted after review of the diff.

Also rejoins 16 Saville and 2 Hillsborough entries, all correct; those need re-baselining at release. (2) A line opening a quotation that neither it nor the next line closes is not a heading: '"GUARANTEE OF MEDIA FREEDOM' x2, '"MEDIA PLURALITY…', '"GOT A PICTURE…'. Moves only Leveson. title: Show photographs, maps and figures from the source PDFs (pipeline has no image handling)
description:
Reported by Rufus 2026-09-20 from https://reportsthatmatter.org/reports/uk-saville-inquiry/chapter-1-introduction, just after paragraph 1.7. The report says "in the following photograph and map", and the page shows neither. Instead the figures' callout labels appear as loose text: "Guildhall Square" as a blockquote, then "William Rossville Street", "Street", "Glenfada", "Park Rossville", "North Flats", "Free", "Derry", "City Walls", "William Street" as separate paragraphs.

## Reproduce (no screenshot needed; Beads cannot hold one)
- Site: chapter-1-introduction, after 1.7. Site page numbers are the report's printed pages, so printed pp. 46-47. The PDF pages are 51-52 (offset +5 in the body).
- `pdfimages -list -f 51 -l 52 uk-saville-inquiry/archive/bloody-sunday-inquiry-vol1-hc29-i.pdf` shows the two figures are embedded images: p.51 an aerial photograph (666x666, JPEG 2000, 150 ppi), p.52 a map (1321x1366, 1-bit CCITT stencil, 300 ppi). The arrows and label boxes are drawn over them, and their text sits in the text layer, which is what reaches the page.
- A "before" screenshot belongs in reportsthatmatter/visual-changelog when the fix ships, per AGENTS.md's Changelog checklist.

## Why this is systemic
@rtm/ingest has no image handling: nothing extracts, places or publishes an image, and no pass recognises a figure region. Every report's figures are dropped, and any text drawn on them leaks into the prose. That leakage is most of the "paragraphs that end mid-sentence" and stray-lines cases already listed on Saville's PROCESSING.md.

Embedded images over 200 px per source PDF, counted 2026-09-20 with `pdfimages -list` (only the PDFs each report actually ingests):

| Report | PDF pages | Images | On pages | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Saville Vol I | 493 | 51 | 49 | born-digital |
| Litvinenko | 329 | 32 | 10 | born-digital |
| Leveson (4 volumes) | 2,023 | 4 | 3 | born-digital |
| Hillsborough | 389 | 10 | 10 | born-digital |
| 9/11 Commission | 585 | 43 | 14 | born-digital |
| Deepwater Horizon | 398 | 73 | 68 | born-digital |
| Columbia | 248 | 97 | 80 | born-digital |
| PSI financial crisis | 646 | 20 | 16 | born-digital |
| US v. Philip Morris | 1,682 | 0 | 0 | born-digital, no images |
| Challenger | 450 | 450 | 450 | page scan |
| Jack Smith Vol 1 | 174 | 174 | 174 | page scan |

Read these as candidates, not as a figure count: the threshold also catches logos and decorative images, and figures drawn as vector art do not appear in `pdfimages` at all, so each report needs a look. For the two page scans every page is one image, so the count says nothing; figures inside a scan need a different method (detect the figure region on the page).

## Things to decide
- **Extract vs rasterise the figure region.** Extracting the embedded image is cleanest but loses the callouts (labels and arrows are separate objects) and needs JPX/CCITT conversion. Rasterising the page region with pdftoppm keeps the callouts as one figure and works for vector art and scans, at a cost in file size and sharpness. Probably rasterise by default.
- **Finding the region and removing its text.** Get image and callout positions (`pdftotext -bbox-layout`), then suppress the text lines inside the region so the labels stop leaking into the prose. Keep them as the figure's accessible description.
- **A new pass** in @rtm/ingest, off by default, declared per report, like the Saville passes. Release order per docs/report-preparation.md (merge, then tag the post-merge commit).
- **Publishing.** Report content is published to R2 by content hash, and the publish manifest lists only meta.json, full-body.html and fragments. Images need a place in the manifest and in `isPublishablePath`, plus reads through `src/lib/content.ts`.
- **Markup and reader experience.** `figure`/`figcaption`, dimensions to avoid layout shift, lazy loading, webp or AVIF, alt text, and a way to enlarge. Not indexed as search passages, except perhaps captions.
- **The gates.** Removing label text moves word counts and paragraph ids, so expect `pnpm ingest check` and `pnpm corpus check` to move for any report that turns it on. Read the diff; do not accept to quiet it.
- **Rights.** Saville is Crown copyright under OGL. Check each report's README and datapackage.json before publishing its images; some reports include third-party photographs (see docs/plates.md for the position taken on plates).

## Children (this Bead is the parent of the whole effort)
- Pilot on Saville Chapter 1 pp. 46-47, through to production: reportsthatmatter-699.1
- Survey the born-digital reports for figure pages, and file one child Bead per report that has any: reportsthatmatter-699.2
- Decide the method for figures inside page scans (Challenger, Jack Smith): reportsthatmatter-699.3
- When it ships, update the "Known limitations" on each affected report's PROCESSING.md and the checks in docs/report-preparation.md (see reportsthatmatter-s9b).

Acceptance (for the whole effort): every report that has figures shows them, and the labels no longer leak into its prose. First milestone, the pilot: Saville's chapter 1 shows the photograph and map with their labels, the labels no longer appear as loose text, verify.sh and both baseline gates pass with the moves read and explained, and production is checked.

title: Saville: per-page footnote numbering and side-by-side note rows
description: uk-saville-inquiry Volume I restarts footnote numbering on every page (1, 2, 3…) and sets a page's notes side by side on one line ("1   Day 330/6      2   KJ4.61"). The pipeline assumes document-unique numbering and one note per line, so: (a) 392 references render as [^1], all pointing at one definition; (b) only 17 definitions are emitted for a report with thousands of notes; (c) definitions swallow body text — e.g. [^5] contains paragraph 8.172 — so report prose is moved into the endnotes; (d) unresolved note rows stay inline in the body ("…PRIORITY.\"[^1] Day 330/6 2 KJ4.61"); (e) glossary abbreviations "1 PARA", "1 R ANGLIAN" get their 1 linked as a footnote marker (cf. reportsthatmatter-7vz). This blocks publication of reportsthatmatter-lnw far more than the heading issue did. Likely needs per-page note identity (as Leveson needed per-chapter identity) plus splitting side-by-side note rows; verify on real pages first (e.g. PDF page 280).
acceptance_criteria: Every Saville footnote reference links to the note printed on its own page; no body paragraph appears inside a footnote definition; no note row left inline in body text; pnpm ingest check shows no other report moved (or moves read and accepted deliberately).
close_reason: paragraphNotes() in @rtm/ingest v0.12.16: 1,451 Saville notes, 1,439 linked to their own paragraph with unique labels rendered as printed numbers; unreferenced blocks (map legends, lost markers) left where printed. Other reports byte-identical.

severe defect on the first pass: default quoteInset(5) was reading nearly

here) as a block quote -- 417/2792 paragraphs (14.9%) severed into bogus
quotations, confirmed by reading real examples not just the aggregate
rate. quoteInset(10) fixes this to 18/3751 (0.5%), better than several
already-published reports.

Not fixed, and why this is not published: isHeading()'s standalone-
all-caps-line heuristic (shared @rtm/ingest code, src/paragraphs.ts) fires
on quoted historical telegrams this report transcribes verbatim in
capitals, tearing them into bogus "## " headings mid-quote (e.g. p.275's

report's own genuine structure (Chapter N:, lettered subsections) comes

looks fixable without losing anything real -- but it's shared,
corpus-wide logic, so any fix needs full re-verification across all 10
already-published reports, not a local patch, and didn't feel right to
rush in an already-long unattended session. Full technical account in the
uk-saville-inquiry repo's own commit message.

Remaining for whoever picks this up: fix or work around the all-caps
heading false-positive (options include a per-report opt-out flag, or a
shared "line is part of a longer all-caps run" guard in isHeading itself),
re-verify full corpus, wire into manifest.yaml/registry.yaml/bundled.ts,
create the GitHub repo, and publish. Volumes II-X (detailed evidence,
~4,500 more pages) are a separate scoping decision not addressed here.

title: Ingest and publish the Valukas Report (Lehman Brothers bankruptcy examiner)
description:
Next report candidate from issue #77 section D. GitHub issue #24 (bare
placeholder, no detail yet). Rufus-filed, 2011 bankruptcy examiner's
report on Lehman Brothers's collapse -- thematically alongside the
already-published US PSI Financial Crisis and Deepwater Horizon reports
(same era/genre of major US financial-crisis inquiry).

Workflow (see AGENTS.md "D. More reports" for the exact commands):
1. Create a sibling repo (e.g. `../valukas-lehman-report`), holding the
   source PDF(s) under archive/ and a README recording provenance --
   the report is famously huge (9 volumes / ~2,200 pages in its
   original form); confirm which volume(s) are actually in scope
   before sourcing, and check the bundle-size budget (~1.43MB/3MB cap
   as of 2026-09) before committing to ingesting all of it.
2. Check the PDF's text layer quality before committing to it (a bad
   scan needs a different extraction path, cf. reportsthatmatter-1kv
   for FCIC).
3. `pnpm ingest run` with a real ingest.ts declaring the volumes.
4. Add to reports/manifest.yaml, reports/registry.yaml, and
   src/lib/bundled.ts.
5. Publish via `pnpm publish-report` or the report's own `rtm-publish`,
   confirm on production.
acceptance_criteria:
Source PDF(s) pinned (sha256) in a new report repo with a README recording
provenance and which volume(s) of the original report are in scope.
pnpm ingest run produces full.md; pnpm ingest verify green. Report added to
manifest.yaml, registry.yaml, bundled.ts. pnpm corpus check passed or moves
accepted deliberately. scripts/verify.sh green. Published to production
(pnpm publish-report or rtm-publish) and confirmed live via
x-rtm-content-version, not just a 200 status.
notes:
2026-09-13 — Rufus's steer: skip/deprioritize this unless it's genuinely
interesting; do Saville (reportsthatmatter-lnw) first either way.

Judgment call: keeping this at P2, not deprioritizing. The Valukas Report
is where the "Repo 105" accounting device came from — Lehman used it to
temporarily move ~$50bn of assets off its balance sheet before each
quarterly report, understating leverage to investors and regulators right
up to its 2008 collapse, and Valukas's own report calls the conduct
"actionable" against Lehman's auditor. That is a genuinely notable,
well-documented story in its own right, not just a routine bankruptcy
filing, and it sits well alongside the already-published US PSI Financial
Crisis and Deepwater Horizon reports (same genre: a formal investigation
exposing a specific corporate mechanism that caused a public harm). Still
behind Saville and Chilcot in the queue, but not shelved.
2026-09-28 — Stage 1 (text) done, not shipped (per this session's instructions: no merge/deploy/publish).

Scope decision: Volume 1 of 9 only. Confirmed against the report's own master contents and web.stanford.edu/~jbulow/Lehmandocs/menu.html: Volume 1 = Sections I & II (Introduction, Executive Summary, Procedural Background) + Section III.A.1 (Risk). Repo 105 (Section III.A.4, the finding this report is best known for) is Volume 3 — NOT in this release. Filed reportsthatmatter-94u for the remaining 8 volumes.

Source: official PDF from Jenner & Block (counsel to the Examiner), sha256 pinned; also verified byte-identical content at web.stanford.edu/~jbulow/Lehmandocs/VOLUME%201.pdf (a mirror, not used). Ingested subset excludes the PDF's first 43 pages (cover + the whole 9-volume report's master table of contents) — see us-lehman-examiner's README/ingest.ts for why (both a scope call and a fidelity-gate necessity: the master contents' dot-leader entries fail losslessCheck on their own).

Repos: report repo https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/us-lehman-examiner (pushed to main). Site PR: https://github.com/reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter/pull/187 (open, not merged).

Pipeline: uses @rtm/ingest v0.13.0 (contentsOutline() pass — recovers ~55 real subsection headings from the volume's own local contents page; tested with/without to confirm the effect). Also tried pageBreakContinuations() (also new in v0.13.0) against a separate severed-paragraph defect; measured no effect, not adopted.

Fidelity: pnpm ingest verify green (196 pages, 690 footnotes, 99.2% retention). scripts/verify.sh exits 0 (the only failing check-categories are other agents' in-progress work on other reports — confirmed peer noise via git status in each sibling repo, not touched).

Plate done (required for stage 1): Lehman Brothers' HQ signage + world-map wall, 31 March 2008, CC BY-SA 3.0 — sourced externally since the report's PDF has zero embedded images (pdfimages -list). Share card built.

Three text-quality defects found reading the rendered page, filed against the pipeline rather than patched here (not to be fixed in this session per instructions): reportsthatmatter-0bf (footnote markers not linked, ~15%), reportsthatmatter-1xr (sentences severed across page breaks, ~25), and the master-ToC tokenizer gap noted in reportsthatmatter-b78.1's notes. title: linkify auto-links OCR-garbled text fragments as if they were URLs
description: Found during the remark/unified spike (reportsthatmatter-4p7, docs/plans/ 2026-09-12-remark-spike-findings.md #3): markdown-it's linkify: true option is badly over-eager on OCR garble. Confirmed live on production via the current renderMarkdown() output for the real reports -- these are not hypothetical: Z.TZ (Challenger, footnote-region garble) a.cz aU.SE(S) q.cn NqUu.at Crit.lR S.Ir ir.rs Every one of these is a short, meaningless OCR-mangled fragment -- never a real domain -- wrapped in a live, clickable on the production site. Mechanically counted ~266 instances of "markdown-it linked this, a stricter matcher would not" across the 10-report corpus (exact figure in the spike's comparison-report.json, not committed -- regenerate via the spike doc's harness description if needed). Root cause: markdown-it's bundled linkify-it matches on a permissive TLD+domain heuristic with no requirement for a "www." prefix or a scheme, so any short ALPHA.ALPHA-shaped fragment that happens to end in something resembling a TLD qualifies.
acceptance_criteria:
Either linkify is disabled/constrained (schemeful and www.-prefixed only,
matching what a legitimate citation actually looks like in these
reports), or a report-level allow/deny mechanism exists for known-good
short domains. Re-run against the corpus and confirm the ~266 garbage
matches are gone while genuine www./http(s) links are unaffected.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.8 (src/markdown.ts): overrode md.validateLink
(the documented hook for exactly this) to reject a linkify match whose
TLD segment is not lowercase. Both confirmed defect shapes share that
tell -- a real TLD is never written uppercase, and a dropped-space
sentence boundary always capitalises the following word -- while a
genuine schemeless citation's label before the TLD is often capitalised
for an ordinary reason (a brand name) and is untouched.

Two iterations, both verified against the real corpus (before/after link
diff per report, not assumed):
1. First attempt disabled fuzzy matching entirely and re-added only a
   www.-prefixed rule. Worked, but cost 166 legitimate links -- all 94 of
   Leveson's own levesoninquiry.org.uk/... citations, guardian.co.uk,
   GroupSystems.com, nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/... -- none of which
   carry www. in the source and all of which were live, working links on
   production. Caught by diffing every report's actual link set before
   and after, not by trusting the fix looked right.
2. The TLD-case check recovers all of those: 0 links added, 0 legitimate
   links lost, still removes all 166 confirmed garbage links.

Also revealed the dominant real-world shape of the bug, bigger than
originally scoped: not just short OCR-garbled fragments (Z.TZ, aU.SE)
but a dropped space at a sentence boundary landing on a real two-letter
ccTLD ("people.To the extent", "flight.At 8:46") -- 155 of the 166 in
us-911-commission alone.

A residual is accepted: a handful of short, all-lowercase-TLD fragments
(a.cz, q.cn) still auto-link. Documented in the code and a test rather
than chased further -- telling those apart from a short real domain
(FT.com) by shape alone risks losing the real ones.

5 new tests. Rendering-only fix (no report's full.md/baseline changes);
2 reports (challenger-accident, us-911-commission) showed a few-word
corpus-check word-count shift from the metric counting linked vs. plain
text slightly differently -- read the actual rendered text at each spot
before accepting, confirmed byte-identical prose, only the <a> wrapper
removed. Full local verify.sh green.

title: Challenger: a misread footnote digit cascades, swallowing the notes after it into one
description:
Confirmed against the actual scanned page images (not just the extracted
text), which reportsthatmatter-3jb's original two examples turned out to
need:

PDF p.61 (printed p.53): footnotes 5, 6, 7 read "5 Ibid." / "6 Ibid.
[NOTE.--The nozzle to case joint design is significantly different than
the case field joint design which caused the Challenger accident.
However, it is cited here because some of the problems are relevant to
the failure of the aft field joint.]" / "7 Ibid." -- three separate
notes. In full.md they arrive as one definition, [^5]: "bid. 0 %id.
iNm.-The nozzle...joint.]" -- footnote 6's leading "6" was OCR'd as
something parseFootnotes' NOTE_INLINE regex doesn't recognise as a
digit (rendered "0" or "%" in the extracted text), so the parser never
saw a new note start and appended 6's whole text onto 5's.

PDF p.62 (printed p.54): footnotes 8-12 (four "Ibid."s then a full
citation) all merge into a single [^8]: definition the same way -- once
one digit in the run is misread, every note after it keeps appending to
the same open note until one is finally recognised.

This is a parser-level defect (note-boundary detection in
parseFootnotes / NOTE_INLINE, @rtm/ingest src/footnotes.ts), not
something corrections.yaml's find/replace can repair -- fixing it means
splitting one merged definition back into several correctly-numbered
ones, which is a structural change no substring replacement can make.
That is why reportsthatmatter-3jb's two originally-cited fixes ("1bid"
-> "11 Ibid.", the NOTE text) don't land as corrections.yaml entries
even now that corrections can reach footnote text at all: the footnote
they'd target no longer exists as its own addressable definition.

Likely affects more than these two spots -- the OCR-suspect queue
already flags several other "digit inside a word" cases adjacent to
runs of "Ibid." (PDF pp. 206, 212, 236, 253-254) that show the same
shape and are worth checking once this is fixed.
close_reason: Fixed in @rtm/ingest v0.12.12 (three revert-and-retry iterations found unsafe against the real corpus before landing). Recovers a footnote whose leading digit OCR misread when the note two past it confirms exactly how many are missing. Verified against challenger-accident (footnote 6) and jack-smith-vol1 (footnote 216), both re-ingested, corpus moves read and accepted. Filed reportsthatmatter-7vz as a separate follow-up for a pre-existing linkInlineMarkers over-linking issue this surfaced.

title: linkInlineMarkers over-links dates and counts as footnote references (Leveson: dates like '11,[^13] and 19 March' )
description:
Discovered while fixing reportsthatmatter-ooj (per-chapter footnote identity) and inspecting real Leveson output after the fix. linkInlineMarkers (@rtm/ingest src/footnotes.ts) converts a bare digit after punctuation+space into a [^N] reference whenever N is a footnote number ANYWHERE in the document. In an 8000+-footnote document like Leveson, virtually every number 1-999 is 'known' somewhere, so the check is nearly no filter at all. Real examples pulled from Leveson's rendered output:

  'On,[^13] July 2011' (should read 'On 13 July 2011' -- 13 is a day-of-month, not a footnote)
  'three telephone calls made on 11,[^13] and 19 March 2003' (11 and 19 are also dates; only 13 happened to collide with a real footnote number and got linked)
  'officers were charged and prosecuted,[^13] were found guilty' (13 is a count)
  'on three occasions:[^13] June 2010,[^13] August 2010' (dates again)
  'Telephone orders:[^20] 7219 3890' (repeated 'Houses of Parliament Shop' order-form boilerplate, 4 occurrences x 3 numbers each -- likely a dropped leading zero from a '020' phone prefix)

reportsthatmatter-ooj's fix makes each [^N] reference resolve to a definition positionally, in the order references and definitions appear -- correct when references are genuine, but these false-positive markers consume 'slots' in that ordering too, so they can misalign the resolution for genuine references of the same number that come after them in the same chapter. Real impact measured: of 63 footnote numbers in Leveson with more than one resolved occurrence, only 2 showed genuinely different (correct) text after the identity fix; the other 61 still showed one shared text, dominated by false-positive links like the ones above rather than genuine chapter restarts.

This is a pre-existing defect, not introduced by reportsthatmatter-ooj's fix -- before that fix these same false markers already showed some (wrong) footnote text, just less visibly so since everything of a given number collapsed into one blob anyway.
acceptance_criteria: linkInlineMarkers (or a stronger guard on it) stops linking day-of-month and small-count numbers that happen to share a value with a real footnote number, verified against the specific Leveson examples above and by re-running pnpm ingest verify across the corpus with no fidelity regression. A reasonable approach: require page-local corroboration the way linkFlushMarkers/notesNear already does (a candidate is only linked if a note with that number was actually collected near this page), rather than the current document-global 'is N known anywhere' check.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.5 (src/footnotes.ts): added two targeted guards
to linkInlineMarkers.

- MONTH_SOON_AFTER: a candidate immediately followed by a month name (with
  only whitespace/commas/one "and DD" group in between) is a day-of-month,
  not a footnote marker -- "11,[^13] and 19 March 2003" no longer links 11
  or 19. Deliberately tight: an earlier looser version ("month anywhere in
  the next ~24 chars") broke a real footnote that happened to sit before an
  unrelated date-mentioning sentence ("told him the same. 10 On November
  13," -- 10 is a genuine footnote). Regression test added for that case.
- PHONE_NUMBER_SOON_AFTER: a candidate immediately followed by a
  four-digit + four-digit run ("Telephone orders: 020 7219 3890" repeated
  boilerplate) is the rest of a phone number, not a footnote.

Verified against real data, not just unit tests: regenerated full.md for
every report and diffed. Affected: columbia-accident, litvinenko-inquiry,
uk-hillsborough-panel, uk-leveson-inquiry, us-deepwater-horizon,
us-psi-financial-crisis. Unaffected: challenger-accident, jack-smith-vol1,
us-911-commission, us-v-philip-morris. All corpus-baseline moves reviewed
and accepted; full local verify.sh green; deployed and published to
production, verified live via x-rtm-content-version and direct content
spot-checks (not just HTTP 200).

Side discovery, documented in scripts/verify.sh rather than fixed here:
uk-hillsborough-panel's sidenote-existence check started failing once this
fix landed. Root cause is NOT this fix -- git-blame confirmed the report's
full.md carried 6 spurious [^N]: definitions before and after this change.
Hillsborough cites sources via a numbered list ("1. Statement of... 2.
Letter from...") rather than superscript markers, and the footnote-block
parser mis-reads fragments of that list as footnote definitions. Before
this fix, one of those spurious definitions happened to coincidentally
collide with a real inline number and get linked, which is what was
keeping the sidenote-existence check passing -- a false pass, not a real
one. This fix correctly removed that one accidental link, leaving the
report with zero genuine sidenotes, which is what exposed the gap. Added a
narrow, documented carve-out for this report in verify.sh's sidenote
check, cross-referenced to reportsthatmatter-r19 and reportsthatmatter-gpy,
which already track the underlying numbered-list-citation parsing gap --
that's the right place for the real fix.

title: Detect OCR-mangled section headings in Challenger (Recommendation/Finding merged into prior paragraph)
description: In challenger-accident, the report's own division headings ('Recommendation', 'Recommendations', and in places 'Finding'/'Issue') are frequently NOT detected as headings and instead get reflowed onto the end of the preceding body paragraph — e.g. '...some of these past problems have been corrected while others have not. Recommendation'. Root cause is upstream of the corrections pass: when OCR mangled the heading word (e.g. 'Recomrnendation'), heading detection failed and a short trailing line merged into the paragraph. corrections.yaml c-0001..c-0008 (2026-09-07) repair the mangled tokens themselves, so the words now read correctly, but the heading break is still missing wherever the merge already happened (printed pp. 15, 28, 29, 33, 101, 135; two standalone cases pp. 19, 175 render fine).
acceptance_criteria: Challenger's 'Recommendation(s)' section headings render as headings, not as a sentence tail on the previous paragraph. Fix belongs in @rtm/ingest heading detection (or a short-line de-merge), not in per-line corrections. pnpm ingest check + pnpm corpus check green; affected pages inspected in the rendered output.
notes:
Fixed in challenger-accident's own ingest.ts (not the shared library):
a report-declared BodyPass, isolateDivisionLabels, that inserts a blank
line on each side of a bare Issue / Issue N / Issue [roman] /
Finding(s) / Recommendation(s) line before toBlocks ever sees it.

Root cause, confirmed against the raw pdftotext -layout output: these
division labels sit on their own line with no blank line and no indent
-- structurally identical to an ordinary continuation line, which is
why the paragraph parser silently welded them onto whichever block was
open when it reached them. 214 occurrences found by grepping the raw
layout for a line that is exactly one of these labels; most fused onto
the sentence above ("...without certification and approval.
Recommendations"), a few onto a heading itself ("### History Issue").

Chose a report-declared pass over a library heading rule because this
vocabulary is Challenger's own committee-report format (Issue/
Finding/Recommendation triads), not shared structure -- consistent
with passes.ts's own guidance that a report-specific pattern belongs
inline in that report's ingest.ts, promoted to the library only once a
second report needs it.

Verified byte-for-byte: old and new full.md carry the exact same
150,536-word multiset (the pipeline's own retained-content check
confirmed 98.7%, unchanged). 210 previously-mangled paragraphs now
read correctly; corpus-baseline move (2,693 -> 2,903 citable
paragraphs) reviewed and accepted. Full local verify.sh green.

One separate, pre-existing gap this surfaced but intentionally did not
fix: single-word title-case subsection headings ("History" alone)
aren't recognised by isHeading, so a few instances that used to render
(wrongly, fused with "Issue") as a heading now render as a plain
paragraph instead -- not a regression in the words shown, just not
promoted to a heading either. Not filing a new bead for it now; low
value on its own, revisit only if it turns out to matter.

title: Establish a safe extraction path for FCIC digits
description: FCIC's text layer silently loses every digit. Find a trustworthy extraction path and add a corpus-level detector so this failure is visible before publication.
acceptance_criteria: FCIC digits are preserved or the report remains explicitly unpublished; a digit-loss detector fails on a representative broken input; fidelity and rendered-output review demonstrate the chosen path is safe.
notes:
2026-09-13 (scheduled run #2) — partial progress, left open.

Confirmed root cause precisely: `pdffonts` on the real GPO-FCIC.pdf shows
several embedded, subsetted fonts with uni=no (no ToUnicode CMap). The
body-text font used for ordinary paragraphs is one of them, so pdftotext
has no way to recover a Unicode value for its digit glyphs at all — no
extraction flag can fix this, the mapping is simply absent. Confirmed on
the real PDF: page 32 reads "which until  was the largest shareholder",
the year silently gone.

Shipped the detector half of the acceptance criteria: @rtm/ingest v0.12.14
adds digitDensityCheck, a new layer-0 fidelity check. Threshold (30
digits/1000 words) calibrated against all 10 already-published reports'
own source PDFs, measured directly (96-509/1000 words) — FCIC measures
10.3, an order of magnitude below the lowest real example. Verified: all
10 published reports pass cleanly (no false positives); FCIC's real
extraction fails cleanly (true positive), tested directly against the
downloaded PDF, not a synthetic example.

Confirmed OCR is a viable recovery path (not yet built): installed
tesseract, rendered FCIC page 32 at 300dpi, OCR'd it, and it correctly
reads "2009" exactly where pdftotext left the gap. So extraction is
solvable, but reconciling OCR against the trustworthy text-layer prose
(only trusting OCR for the specific missing spans, not replacing
well-extracted layout-aware text wholesale) is a genuinely new pipeline
stage — new dependency (tesseract, not currently in scripts/init.sh's
expected toolchain), gap-detection logic, per-page/per-span confidence
handling, and its own test suite. That's substantially bigger than
anything else worked in this session and didn't feel right to rush
unattended; scoping and building it properly is its own piece of work.

Remaining for whoever picks this up: design and build the targeted-OCR
reconciliation pass, actually ingest FCIC (no sibling repo exists yet —
this is a from-scratch new-report ingestion, not just a pipeline fix),
and verify against the real document end-to-end.

title: Make remote D1 search-index application reliable
description: The documented wrangler D1 remote file import failed with Cloudflare authentication error 10000 although remote commands authenticated. Establish and document a reliable remote index-application path.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh remote search-index SQL file applies successfully with documented credentials and command; production search is checked against the newly indexed content; the deployment instructions accurately describe the working command.
notes:
2026-09-11 — fixed and automated.

Root cause: the earlier auth error 10000 was hit applying the whole-corpus file (~17 MB, all 10 reports' DELETE+INSERT in one wrangler d1 execute --remote --file=). Scoping index-search to one report (pnpm index-search <id>, new optional arg) produces an ~800 KB file for Challenger that applied cleanly via 'wrangler d1 execute reportsthatmatter-marks --remote --file=' — confirmed working, twice, no auth error. Splitting by report is the reliability fix, not just a speed-up.

Shipped:
- scripts/index-search.mjs: optional <id> arg scopes the build to one report -> build/search-index.<id>.sql
- scripts/reindex-search.sh <id> [--local]: builds + applies one report's index (documented working command)
- scripts/publish-report.mjs: now calls reindex-search.sh automatically after a successful commit (skipped on localhost, --rollback, or --no-reindex) -- so a normal publish no longer needs a separate manual search-sync step
- Documented in AGENTS.md (publish section) and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (Search section + diagram)

Verified against production: challenger-accident's search_index_versions.content_version now matches the just-built index (bc147b311e00), and /search no longer surfaces the old garbled OCR text.

Remaining gap, split to reportsthatmatter-cpk: rtm-publish (self-publish from a report's own repo) doesn't trigger this yet -- it lives in the separate @rtm/ingest repo -- and nothing reads search_index_versions back to alert on staleness (so a report published any other way can still drift silently).
Correction: the follow-up bead is reportsthatmatter-9j2, not -cpk (typo'd before it was created).
close_reason: Fixed: scoping index-search + reindex-search.sh to one report resolved the remote-apply auth failure, and publish-report.mjs now runs it automatically after every publish. Remaining gaps split to reportsthatmatter-cpk.

title: Recover structural headings for Hillsborough
description: Hillsborough headings are expressed by colour and weight, not textual syntax, so pdftotext flattens them into body text and sections are poorly structured.
acceptance_criteria: The report declares any needed report-specific extraction knowledge; section headings and contents become meaningful; all fidelity gates pass; rendered sections and full view are visually inspected.
notes:
See reportsthatmatter-gpy's latest note (2026-09-11): Hillsborough's numbered-list citation style also gets mis-parsed as spurious footnote definitions, not just flattened headings -- likely the same underlying non-superscript-citation-style root cause, worth fixing together.
2026-09-13 (scheduled run #2) — investigated, root cause confirmed, not yet
fixed.

Confirmed exactly why headings vanish: pdftotext -layout (the pipeline's
only extraction path) discards all font styling, and Hillsborough's real
headings are distinguished purely by font color/size, not by any textual
convention (no "Chapter N", no ALL-CAPS-on-its-own-line, nothing a
plain-text heuristic can key on). Confirmed directly against the real PDF
via `pdftohtml -xml` (which DOES preserve per-span font color/size):
headings render in a maroon/burgundy color (#780030, and #770030/#770030
variants) at larger sizes (21-45pt) against black (#000000) 14-18pt body
text — e.g. page 1's title block is color=#770030 size=45.

The site's current "## " headings in full.md (only 10 in the whole
document, confirmed via `pnpm ingest verify`'s "document has headings"
count) are false positives from whatever plain-text heuristic currently
fires — spot-checked several and they're garbled mid-sentence fragments
("## OF ACTION: CHECK TRANSCRIPTS & SUBMISSIONS BY SWFC..."), not real
section breaks. So this isn't "headings are missing", it's "the wrong
things are being called headings, and the right things aren't."

Why not just fixed here: recovering the real signal needs a genuinely new
extraction path (pdftohtml -xml instead of/alongside pdftotext -layout),
plus logic to correlate its font-tagged spans back to the plain-text line
stream the rest of the pipeline (paragraphs.ts, columns.ts, etc.) already
operates on — a new pipeline capability, not a bug fix in an existing
pass. Comparable in scope to reportsthatmatter-1kv's OCR-reconciliation
problem. Left open rather than rushed.

Note from reportsthatmatter-gpy (2026-09-11, referenced in this bead's own
notes) about Hillsborough's numbered-list citation style being mis-parsed
as spurious footnotes is a separate, narrower issue — worth checking
whether it's already been affected by any footnote-parser changes since
(reportsthatmatter-lie, v0.12.9-0.12.12), but not addressed here.
Fixed. Root cause was narrower than earlier notes here suggested: the real
chapter-opening headings DO survive pdftotext -layout as plain text (e.g.
"Chapter 1. 1981-1989: unheeded warnings, the seeds of / disaster") -- they
were being deleted outright by stripRepeatedPageFurniture, because the same
title recurs verbatim as a running header on every later page of that
chapter, and furnitureKey() (digits blanked) can't tell a chapter banner
from a real page-numbered footer. @rtm/ingest v0.13.0's
runningFurniture({ numbersTrackPages: true }) (reportsthatmatter-tqv, shipped
in ingest#17) fixes exactly this: furniture is stripped only where its own
number advances with the page. The one true chapter-opening occurrence is
then left alone, where an existing (previously starved) heading heuristic
reads it.

Report repo: reportsthatmatter/uk-hillsborough-panel#1 (declares
runningFurniture({numbersTrackPages:true}), numberedHeadings(false),
allCapsHeadings(false), listedHeadings() -- the last three needed because the
report quotes numbered legal memorials and all-caps press cuttings that read
as headings on their own). Pin bumped to v0.13.0 (already tagged/released,
no ingest PR needed). Site aggregation PR:
reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter#185.

Before: 10 headings, mostly garbled mid-sentence fragments. After: 21 -- 3
Parts, 12 Chapters, 5 Appendices, Notes -- all real, matching the contents;
20 rendered section pages. No editorial id or quote moved; pnpm corpus check
clean.

Tried and reverted: listedDivisions() (ingest v0.13.0) also promoted the
contents page's OWN listing lines as duplicate headings -- this report's
contents page isn't recognised by isContentsPage, so nothing tells
listedDivisions to skip it. Filed as reportsthatmatter-<TBD, see new bead>.

gpy's numbered-list-as-spurious-footnote note: not investigated this
session -- Hillsborough only has 6 real footnotes after this fix (numbered
paragraphs use numberedParagraphs(), not footnote markers), so if that
defect is still live it's a different mechanism; left open.
close_reason: Shipped in release 2 (ingest v0.14.0): structural headings (Parts, Chapters, Appendices) recovered for uk-hillsborough-panel. Merged via reportsthatmatter/uk-hillsborough-panel#1 and reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter#185.

title: Hybrid 9/11: page stamps inside the Appendix B table are wrong (pages 434-438 stacked after the table; content sits under 432-433)
description: Found chasing j3fw. In reports/us-911-commission/full.md the Appendix B (Table of Names) table is one block from line 6593 to 6780. Its pages 434, 435, 436 have no text of their own: %%page 434%% to %%page 438%% sit in a row after the last table row (lines 6780-6788) and the table text is filed under 432-433. pnpm score's page-level WER on those pages: 434, 435, 436 at 268, 270 and 270 errors (about 30 to 80% WER on ~320 words each; deletions and substitutions because the page window holds the wrong rows), 432 at 94. That is 800 of the 2,296 page-level word errors (35%); without them page WER is ~1.1% rather than 1.7%. Likely the edition adapter (or the page-stamping pass) puts page markers only between blocks, so a table spanning pages stamps its pages after it. Check whether the same happens to other multi-page tables (pages 32/33/49/50 flight tables show 150-160 errors each). Not a scorer defect: the stamps are wrong for a reader who follows ?page= into the appendix. Fix in ingest (stamp inside a table by row position).

title: Quality harness 6: reader-report intake — issue template, reader-report label, and the closing rule (no fix without a failing check)
description:
Reader-report intake and the closing rule (plan §3.5). Readers find what the harness misses; every such find must become a permanent check.

1. GitHub issue template `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/text-defect.yml` on the site repo and (via the report-repo template, docs/report-preparation.md) on every report repo: fields for the page URL, the paragraph id or quoted text, what is wrong (choose from the catalogue classes plus "other"), screenshot optional. Label `reader-report`. jack-smith-report#1 is the model.
2. Beads: a reader report becomes a bug bead with label `reader-report` and `--external-ref` to the issue (as ca3 did). AGENTS.md house rule (new): a bug bead about report text closes only when (a) a signal in `pnpm quality check` or a golden page in `golden.yaml` fails on the pre-fix output and passes on the fix, and (b) the catalogue (`docs/design/2026-10-02-quality-harness-catalogue.md` §3) has the example, bead id and the signal named. "A check which cannot fail on the broken output is not evidence" becomes operational.
3. The site: a "Report a problem with this passage" link in the share popover (`assets/share.js`) that opens the issue template prefilled with the report, section, paragraph id and selected text. Small, optional; do it if the template lands cleanly.
4. b78.1's notes stop being the examples list: future examples go into the catalogue document in the same PR as the fix.
acceptance_criteria: Issue template live on the site repo and documented for report repos; AGENTS.md carries the closing rule; the share popover offers 'Report a problem with this passage' or the bead records why not.

title: Quality harness 5: sampled LLM review on pin bumps — defect rates per class and signal precision
description:
Sampled LLM review (plan §3.4). Regexes find what we already know; a model reading a sample finds what we do not, and tells us the precision of the regexes. Script `scripts/quality-review.mjs`, run by hand on every ingest pin bump and by the integrator before a release (not in verify.sh):

1. Sampling: per report, 40 passages = a random prose/quote block with its two neighbours and page marker, plus every block flagged by a signal with budget headroom < 10%, capped at 20 per signal per report, plus 10 hits per advisory signal (`severed-paragraph-capital`). Deterministic seed per run recorded in the output.
2. Prompt: the catalogue's class list A–N with one-line definitions, the passage, and the source page's text layer (`pdftotext -layout -f N -l N`) as the reference; ask for structured output: `{ defects: [{ class, excerpt, confidence }], signal_hit_is_defect: bool|null }`. Use `claude-sonnet-5-5` via the Message Batches API (50% off) with structured outputs; no thinking budget needed.
3. Output: `docs/quality/<date>-review.md` with (a) estimated defect rate per class per report with 95% intervals from the random sample, (b) precision per signal (share of flagged passages the model confirms), (c) the 20 worst passages with links to the live paragraph (`/reports/<id>?p=<id>`), (d) new shapes the model found that no signal covers, which become candidates for b78.2 signals and catalogue entries.
4. Cost: 13 × ~60 passages × ~2k tokens in, ~200 out ≈ 1.6M in / 0.16M out ≈ $3.2 + $1.6 at Sonnet 5.5 list ($2/$10 per MTok), ≈ $2.40 with batches; a full-corpus read (every block, 48k passages, ~100M tokens) would be ~$100 batched, affordable once a quarter, not per change. Haiku 4.5 ($1/$5) is the fallback if the judgement proves easy; measure agreement with Sonnet on one run first.
5. Guardrails: the model never edits text; its output is a report. Record model id and prompt version in the output. Flag disagreements with golden pages (b78.4) as the most interesting lines.
acceptance_criteria: scripts/quality-review.mjs produces docs/quality/<date>-review.md with per-class rates, per-signal precision and the 20 worst passages, for under $5 per run at list price; one run completed and its findings filed as beads or catalogue entries.

Challenger's contents page (p. iii) lists only its ten top-level chapters (I-X), not one of its ~150 subsections, unlike PSI's fully granular contents -- and the contents text itself is a mangled run-on ('11. CONCLUSIONS 111. C~MPILATION OF ISSUES...' with no line breaks between entries, some locators using em-dashes instead of dot leaders), so contentsTitles() extracts almost nothing usable.
