title: [bug] us-psi-financial-crisis: notes that run over whole pages still print in the body (~17 paragraphs)
description: Left after reportsthatmatter-je7 (@rtm/ingest v0.12.20), which fixed the note counter and removed all duplicate definitions. 20 body paragraphs still carry a citation marker; 3 are genuine chart source captions ('Prepared by the U.S. Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations... Derived from Goldman Sachs document'), the rest are footnote text. Main shape: a note long enough to fill most of the next page or two, e.g. PDF pp.438-439 are entirely the continuation of one note (Bear Stearns markdowns, 'BSAM mark recap', with a block quotation inside the note), so the page has no numbered note block for splitPage to find. Also: '6/7/2007 email exchange between Mr. Swenson and Mr. Lehman, "BSAM Post"', 'GS MBS-E-013746511 (discussing "what would happen upon an ACA bankruptcy', 'Subcommittee QFR at PSI_QFR_GS0249'. Measure: paragraphs matching /SCO-|GS MBS-E|Hearing Exhibit|Int\. Tr\.|HSC Tr\./ after stripping [^N].
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest citationRunOver() (opt-in pass, unreleased):
reportsthatmatter/ingest#20. Report repo: reportsthatmatter/us-psi-financial-crisis#4
(DO-NOT-MERGE until ingest#20 ships and the pin bumps off v0.12.20). Site
aggregation PR: reportsthatmatter/reportsthatmatter#184.

Root cause: a note's run-over may be several ordinary single-spaced
paragraphs (a quotation, its source line, more prose), not one unbroken
double-spaced run, so the existing g1f/je7 run-over check never fired.
citationRunOver walks upward from a found footnote block's start and rescues
a paragraph only while it is itself dense with this report's own citation
style (Bates numbers, hearing exhibits) -- content, not whitespace, is what
tells a footnote's overflow from body prose here. A first attempt keyed on
blank-line gap width instead and moved a real heading ("D. Ratings
Deficiencies") into a footnote; reverted for the content-based check.

Measured (paragraphs matching /SCO-|GS MBS-E|Hearing Exhibit|Int. Tr.|HSC
Tr./ after stripping [^N], excluding 3 genuine chart-source captions): 17
leaked footnote paragraphs before, 3 after. Remaining 3 (pp.449 x2, 497) are
a different, narrower shape -- a note's defining text displaced mid-page by
an embedded chart, not a page-crossing run-over. Filed as a follow-up.

pnpm corpus check clean; no editorial id or quote moved.

title: challenger-accident: six body paragraphs are footnote text (Ibid runs)
description: Swept 2026-09-25 (reportsthatmatter-g1f): 6 of 2,845 Challenger paragraphs open like a footnote and carry two or more citation shapes, e.g. 101-ibid-volume-i-p ('101 Ibid., Volume I, p. 170. 102 Ibid., p. 174.'), 107-ibid-p-5-38-lo8, see-also-cmte-hgs-transcri, ibid-p-1052-see-also. The scan's footnote blocks on those pages are not detected (OCR noise in the note numbers: 'lo8', '* O Q'). Also: a table footnote '1 Continued from June 17, Morton Thiokol only.' in the hearings list now shows as its own plain paragraph (before g1f it hid behind a bogus [^1] link). Philip Morris has one similar paragraph (pm3000540103-540118-0107-0116-us-88649). Lower priority: not on a landing page.
acceptance_criteria: Those paragraphs become notes or are recorded as unfixable in PROCESSING/fidelity; corpus diffs read; verify.sh passes.
notes:
All 6 body paragraphs plus the Philip Morris one confirmed still present, matching the ids in the description (101-ibid-volume-i-p, 107-ibid-p-5-38-lo8, ibid-p-1052-see-also, and the '1 Continued from June 17, Morton Thiokol only.' table footnote). Root cause: these are footnote-block text the footnote-block detector fails to recognise as notes -- in two cases (107.../lo8, * O Q) because the note numbers are themselves OCR-garbled and break the sequential-number check; in the '101...102' case the numbers are clean but it still isn't caught (not fully root-caused -- possibly a short remaining page, similar to g1f's fix but not the same shape). Recorded as unfixable this session rather than building a shared footnote-block fix under uncertain corpus-wide blast radius; see reportsthatmatter-b78.1 for the catalogued example. corpus diffs read: these paragraphs are unaffected by the c1y/m2y changes made in the same branch (pnpm ingest check / pnpm corpus check clean for challenger-accident). verify.sh not blocked by this -- no check currently catches footnote-text-as-body-paragraph as a failure.
Release 2 (ingest v0.14.0): not fixed. No pass in this release targets footnote-text-as-body-paragraph (Ibid runs); verified after re-ingest that all three described examples are still present verbatim in full.md (101/102 Ibid at line 2855, 107/lo8/* O Q Ibid at line 2977, Ibid p.1052 at line 3579). Left open.
2026-10-02: one fix attempt made, none shipped. Now 29 body paragraphs open like footnote text with Ibid/citation shapes (the bead's 6 was a narrow sweep). Cause confirmed: the page's footnote block is not found because its numbers are OCR-garbled ('1*0', "1'1", 'Ira', 'e2', 'lo8', '87' for 67), and chooseBlockStart wants the expected next number or a run of three. Consequence beyond the stray paragraphs: such a paragraph sits between a quotation and its page-top tail and blocks the join (printed p.249-250 'Mr. MULLOY...' / '> ria relative to temperatures' stays split). Idea not built: an opt-in fallback in splitFootnoteBlock taking a trailing run of 'garbled-token + 2-3 spaces + text' lines as notes under unreferenceable labels (the number lookup in withSidenotes consumes definitions by number from the front, so a note numbered 87 defined early would be shown at the real note 87's marker; do not number them from the OCR). Left open.

title: jack-smith-vol1: footnote leftovers after g1f — OCR-misnumbered note 129 in body; '20OC00163' read as note 20; unlinked markers '5°' and '55-a'

title: Trial per-report processing notes on Saville Vol I
description:
Trial of reportsthatmatter-wl0 on one report before rolling it out. Saville Vol I is the pilot: it has the richest known-limitations list (12 notes not linked in text, two "note 2" rows on p.234, ~50 page-break splits tracked in q0m, ~140 map-label mid-sentence endings) and was just ingested, so the facts are fresh.

Build, in uk-saville-inquiry:
- PROCESSING.md with a machine-derived facts block (pages, notes linked of total, ingest switches on, corrections applied, fidelity queue size, @rtm/ingest version) and a hand-written "Known limitations" section.
- The README links to it; README stays the source and build description.
- A published per-report page on the site (e.g. /reports/uk-saville-inquiry/processing) linked from the report page. Public wording only, no Bead ids.

Then judge: is it useful to a reader, cheap to keep current, and honest? Record the answer here.

Acceptance:
- Saville page live and verified against production.
- Decision recorded on the README-vs-PROCESSING.md question and on generated-vs-hand-written split.
- If it looks good: one Bead per other report (Jack Smith, Litvinenko, Leveson, Hillsborough, 9/11, Challenger, Columbia, Deepwater Horizon, PSI, Philip Morris), each blocked by this one. If not, close wl0 with the reason.
notes: Verdict 2026-09-20: it works. Live and verified against production (verify.sh passes; Saville text version unchanged). Decisions: (1) separate PROCESSING.md, not a README section: the site publishes exactly one file per report, and the README is AI-written too, so the human-vs-generated argument did not hold; the real reason is that it is the published file. (2) Served from deploy assets, not R2, so it ships with a deploy, not publish-report. (3) Facts block still typed by hand; see the generate-facts follow-up. Follow-ups filed under wl0 for the other ten reports.
close_reason: Saville PROCESSING.md live at /reports/uk-saville-inquiry/processing (PR #144), verified against production

notes: zphc (2026-10-02): the inquiry HTML (report.bloody-sunday-inquiry.org, UKGWA/Wayback) covers every volume in the same class-annotated form as Vol I, so once ivg.2 (Saville from HTML) works, Vols II-X are mostly a fetch-and-mirror job. gov.uk page counts: II 353, III 503, IV 386, V 659, VI 630, VII 661, VIII 591, IX 258, X 546 (4,587), plus Principal conclusions HC 30 (63). Mirror locally (UKGWA blocks scripts; Wayback throttles).

title: Reader-facing summaries and excerpts for each report
description:
Idea from Rufus, 2026-09-20. Needs refinement before building.

Today a report page has the full text plus a short intro. Idea: write our own more accessible layer for readers arriving cold: why the report matters, what it found, and a fuller summary and/or curated excerpts page.

Considerations:
- Tension with the "evidence-first, no commentary" stance in docs/ROADMAP.md. Summaries must be clearly labelled as ours and visibly separate from the report's own text.
- Every claim in a summary should cite back to paragraph ids in the report (paragraph permalinks already exist), so the summary is a way into the text, not a replacement.
- Overlaps with existing curated passages (docs/share-quotes.yaml, highlights template). An excerpts page could grow from those.
- Could be LLM-drafted but human-reviewed before publishing; decide the review bar.
- Big reports (Saville, Leveson) need it most; short ones least.
- Distinct from the per-report processing notes idea; do not merge them, since one is editorial and the other is provenance.

Open questions: summary length and structure; where it lives (sibling repo file vs site); one pilot report to try it on (Saville Vol I is a good candidate: 489 pages, long, high public interest).

Acceptance: a decision on format and review process, then a pilot on one report as a follow-up Bead.
close_reason: Decided; superseded by reportsthatmatter-g0w

comments.author: Rufus Pollock
comments.text: 2026-09-25: format and review decisions made in docs/plans/2026-09-25-reader-layer-and-launch.md; work continues under epic reportsthatmatter-g0w.

title: Per-report processing notes: record and publish how each report was processed
description:
Idea from Rufus, 2026-09-20, after the Saville Vol I ingest. Needs refinement before building.

Problem: the status of a report's processing (what the pipeline fixed, what is still wrong, what is deliberately left alone) currently lives in the session summary in chat, the ingest.ts config, fidelity.md (OCR review queue only) and scattered Beads. Nothing per-report says "here is the honest state of this edition".

Proposal to refine:
- A small per-report file in the report's sibling repo (e.g. PROCESSING.md, next to README.md / fidelity.md / corrections.yaml), because a report owns its own build.
- Two layers: (1) machine-derived facts (page count, footnote count and how many are linked, ingest switches turned on, corrections applied, fidelity queue size, @rtm/ingest version); (2) short human-written "known limitations" prose (e.g. Saville: 12 notes not linked in text; two "note 2" rows on p.234; ~140 mid-sentence endings from map labels).
- Published on the site as a per-report page (e.g. /reports/<id>/processing or an "About this edition" link from the report page), copied in like full.md so a cold clone still builds.
- Publish a dated snapshot, not live Bead status, which goes stale. Do not link internal Bead ids on the public page; describe the limitation instead.
- Fits the site's trust story: readers can see exactly how faithful the text is and where it is not.

Open questions: generated vs hand-written split; whether the fidelity gate should check the file exists; page name and placement; whether to backfill the other ten reports.

Acceptance: a decision recorded on scope, then a follow-up build Bead.
notes: 2026-09-20: Rufus asked whether this should live in README.md instead of a new file. Leaning: separate PROCESSING.md, README links to it (README = source + build, hand-written and stable; processing = partly generated, changes each ingest, and is the one file the site publishes). To be confirmed by the Saville trial.

title: Rejoin paragraphs split at a page break before a capitalised word
description: About 50 long paragraphs in uk-saville-inquiry (and 137 in Litvinenko) end mid-sentence at a page break because mergeAcrossPages only joins when the next page opens lowercase ("…Block 2 of the Rossville" / "Flats. Patrick Campbell…"). Tried 2026-09-18: in numberedParagraphs reports, join whenever the next page doesn't open a numbered paragraph. Reverted: it swallowed subsection headings at page tops and moved Litvinenko, Leveson and Hillsborough. A viable version must exclude headings (e.g. run after contentsHeadings, or require the previous paragraph's page to end without a blank line).
acceptance_criteria: Fewer page-break splits in Saville with no heading lost; pnpm ingest check moves in other reports read and accepted deliberately.
notes: 2026-09-28: pageBreakSplits (ingest#15) counts capitalised page-break continuations as candidates (kind 'capitalised'). Current per report: leveson 643, 911 292, philip-morris 245, deepwater 147, litvinenko 128, psi 109, challenger 66, columbia 37, saville 36, jack-smith 34→36, hillsborough 33. pageBreakContinuations deliberately does not join these.

title: Retire Challenger p. 204 footnote-63 OCR suspect
description: After the parser can recover the printed p. 204 footnote run as 56–63, rebuild Challenger and record the reviewed 8s token as resolved. This task is intentionally separate so the parser bug blocks only this one suspect, not the rest of reportsthatmatter-agk.
acceptance_criteria: Challenger renders footnote 63 as Ibid. and links its inline 63 marker; 8s leaves fidelity.md through a documented correction/dismissal outcome; ingest, corpus, rendered-page, publish, and production checks pass.

title: Recover OCR-garbled sequential footnote runs without guessing
description: On Challenger printed p. 204 (PDF p. 212), the scan clearly contains footnotes 56 through 63. The text layer yields 56, 67, a continuation read as "rigid,", 6 9, 6 0, 6 1, 6*, and 8s. Current @rtm/ingest v0.12.14 parses this as definitions 56, 67, and 8; report-owned corrections cannot change a definition identity after parsing. Extend sequential recovery only where neighboring clean evidence proves the whole run, preserving the no-guess safety rule established by reportsthatmatter-lie.
acceptance_criteria: A failing test built from the real p. 204 footnote lines demonstrates the current 56/67/8 parse. The parser then recovers definitions 56–63 with text matching the scan, while existing ambiguous-run and full-corpus tests remain green. Challenger adopts the released version, its generated/corpus diff is reviewed, and no unrelated report moves.
notes: 2026-09-18 — Rufus approved the recommended exact pre-parse source-line pass design, while explicitly deprioritising this painful one-by-one Challenger cleanup behind higher-value work. Preserve this design for later; do not start it ahead of P2 work.

title: Let an expanded footnote be collapsed again
description: Rufus (GitHub #111): expanding a footnote (sidenote) has no way to collapse it again. Check the footnote expand/collapse interaction in assets/share.js or wherever sidenote toggling lives; needs a toggle rather than one-way expand.
acceptance_criteria: A reader can expand a footnote and collapse it again via the same control; behaviour checked in a browser, not just unit tests; scripts/verify.sh green.

title: Rethink page-number placement beside paragraphs
description: Rufus (GitHub #110): the printed-page-number markers on the side of paragraphs are unclear as-is — he suggested something like the word 'page' in front of the number so it reads unambiguously. Needs a design decision on the exact treatment (label text, placement, styling) before implementing; check src/templates/report.ts and assets/styles.css for how page anchors currently render.
acceptance_criteria: Page-number markers beside paragraphs are unambiguous at a glance (e.g. labelled 'page N' or equivalent); rendered pages visually inspected; scripts/verify.sh green.

title: linkInlineMarkers over-links common single-digit numbers into OCR noise
description:
Discovered while fixing reportsthatmatter-lie (Challenger footnote 5/6/7
cascade). Once a footnote number is "known" (has a real definition),
linkInlineMarkers converts every bare occurrence of that digit in the
right punctuation context into [^N] — including hits inside pure OCR
noise, not just real citations. Confirmed in challenger-accident/full.md
after recovering footnote 6 as its own definition: 23 new [^6] links
appeared, several clearly wrong, e.g.

  "...not always based on sound engineering or scientific principles.[^6] 4 - 4 2 0 0 - 86 - 2"
  (a NASA document-ID fragment, not a citation)

  "June 25, 1986 ..........[^6] ............... Maj. Donald..."
  (a dot-leader table-of-contents/witness-list line)

This isn't new to number 6 specifically — footnote numbers 5 and 7 in the
same document already carry 19 and 10 occurrences respectively (some
presumably legitimate per-chapter restarts, some likely the same noise
pattern), so this is a pre-existing, systemic weakness of
linkInlineMarkers's "known number" heuristic in heavily OCR-garbled
documents, not something the reportsthatmatter-lie fix introduced — it
just made the existing risk visible for one more number.

Not fixed as part of reportsthatmatter-lie: correctly recovering the
merged footnote definition was the actual reported bug and is verified
correct (all fidelity gates green, corpus move read and accepted). This
over-linking is a distinct, separable problem in a different function
(linkInlineMarkers in @rtm/ingest src/footnotes.ts) that needs its own
design thought — likely something like requiring more context around the
digit (e.g. it must not sit inside a long run of digit/punctuation
fragments) before trusting a bare-digit link, not a quick patch.
acceptance_criteria:
A documented false-positive rate (or a fixed heuristic) for linkInlineMarkers
on at least challenger-accident; re-verify against the corpus that any fix
does not regress genuine per-chapter-restart citations (numbers 5 and 7 in
challenger-accident are a live example to check against). Full corpus
re-ingested and any moved ids read and accepted deliberately.

title: Migrate report rendering from markdown-it to remark/unified
description:
Not urgent -- the current pipeline works, verified extensively this
session (reportsthatmatter-ooj, reportsthatmatter-axw, reportsthatmatter-hzf).
This is the scoped follow-up to the spike (reportsthatmatter-4p7), which
recommended migrating eventually for real, verified reasons (remark-gfm's
footnote parsing correctly handles restart-per-chapter reused identifiers;
markdown-it's linkify over-links OCR garble) but found real risks that
must be handled first, not assumed away.

Full findings and a concrete pre-migration checklist:
docs/plans/2026-09-12-remark-spike-findings.md
acceptance_criteria:
Every item in the spike doc's §6 checklist is done: singleTilde: false
configured; the footnote-swallowed-into-autolink bug (§4) fixed and
re-verified against every report's own citation-to-URL spacing
convention, not just Deepwater Horizon; a decision made and documented
on schema-less bare-domain autolinks (§3); the migration ships alongside
(or after) reportsthatmatter-ru3's id-scoping fix, not before it, so the
new pipeline doesn't inherit the bug it's meant to replace. Full corpus
re-ingested, every moved id read and accepted deliberately
(pnpm corpus accept, never waved through), pnpm ingest check and
verify.sh green.

title: An empty bullet-list item borrows unrelated later text for its permalink id
description:
Found during the remark/unified spike (reportsthatmatter-4p7, docs/plans/
2026-09-12-remark-spike-findings.md #5). @rtm/ingest src/markdown.ts's
list-id assignment:

  const firstItem = tokens.slice(i).find((later) => later.type === "inline");

is not scoped to the list's own item -- it searches ALL tokens from the
list-open token onward. A list with a genuinely empty first item (a bare
"-" on its own line, common in OCR-garbled figure/diagram captions --
confirmed example: Challenger page 184, a figure caption reduced to a
lone "-" immediately followed by the heading "## DOWNSTREAM SECONDARY")
has no inline token of its own, so .find() walks past it and grabs the
next inline token anywhere later in the document -- here, the heading
four elements on. The list's permalink id becomes "downstream-secondary",
borrowed from unrelated heading text, contradicting the code's own
documented intent ("its id comes from its first item").

Confirmed via the spike's remark prototype, which correctly scopes to
the list's own children and instead falls back to the documented "para"
default for the same input -- the discrepancy between the two outputs is
what exposed this.
acceptance_criteria:
The list-id lookup is scoped to the list's own subtree (its own first
item's inline content), not the whole remaining token stream. An empty
first item falls back to the same "para"-prefixed default a paragraph
with no usable words gets. Re-ingest affected reports, read the
corpus-baseline diff (ids will move for lists that were previously
mis-assigned), and accept deliberately.
close_reason: Fixed in @rtm/ingest v0.12.13: the list-id lookup is now bounded to the first list_item's own subtree instead of searching unbounded past it. Verified against the exact real case (Challenger PDF p.184's figure caption reduced to a lone '-'), now correctly gets id 'para-2' instead of borrowing 'downstream-secondary'. Corpus moves in challenger-accident, columbia-accident, and us-deepwater-horizon (all 'same count, different ids' — cascading disambiguation-counter shifts from correcting a handful of genuinely-empty list items in each) read and accepted deliberately.

title: Spike: remark/unified instead of markdown-it for report rendering
description: Prototype and full-corpus diff, per GitHub issue #114. See docs/plans/2026-09-12-remark-spike-findings.md for the complete writeup.
acceptance_criteria: A written recommendation exists, backed by a prototype run against all 10 ingested reports with every difference categorized, not eyeballed.
notes: Spin-off beads filed: reportsthatmatter-yhb (linkify false-positive autolinks on OCR garble, live on production today) and reportsthatmatter-ru3 (empty bullet-list item borrows unrelated later text for its permalink id). Both found only by building and diffing a second, independent renderer -- neither is caused by remark itself.

title: corrections.yaml cannot reach footnote-definition text (only body paragraphs/quotes/lists)
description: Discovered while reviewing Challenger's footnote-apparatus OCR suspects (reportsthatmatter-agk, 2026-09-11). applyCorrections' find/replace only searches paragraph/quote/list body blocks; text inside a rendered footnote-definition block (the '[^N]: ...' lines) is never reachable, confirmed empirically — plain unambiguous substrings that visibly exist in that exact rendered text never match as a correction find, while the same text matches fine when it happens to sit in ordinary body prose instead. Two confirmed-correct fixes in Challenger could not be applied because of this: footnote 11 ('1bid' -> '11 Ibid.', PDF p.62) and footnote 6's editorial note ('iNm' -> '[NOTE.-The nozzle...]', PDF p.61), both verified word-for-word against the page image.
acceptance_criteria: Either corrections.yaml gains a documented way to target footnote-definition text (a new scope, or applyCorrections searches Footnote[] too), or the limitation is documented clearly enough that reviewers stop losing time on it. The two Challenger fixes above land once fixed.
notes:
Fixed via @rtm/ingest v0.12.6 (src/corrections.ts, src/pipeline.ts):
applyCorrections now takes an optional fourth argument, footnotes:
Footnote[] (default [], so every existing three-arg call is
unaffected), and searches/replaces within note.text exactly as it
already did for a block's text. The "must match exactly once"
guarantee now counts across blocks and footnotes together, since a
find isn't told in advance which side its text sits on. Footnote
gained an optional printed field (populated the same way a Block's
own provenance is) so where: { volume, printed } scoping works
identically whether the target text is in the body or a note.
pipeline.ts threads the corrected footnotes through the rest of the
build in place of the pre-correction array. 4 new tests in
tests/corrections.test.ts cover the reach, the page-scoping, and the
cross-collection ambiguity check. Full ingest check across all 10
reports confirmed zero side effects from every report's corrections
now also scanning footnote text (none currently target it).

The two Challenger fixes this bead was filed to unblock do NOT land as
corrections.yaml entries, even now that the mechanism reaches them.
Checked against the actual scanned page images (not just the
extracted text) rather than trust the original investigation's text-
only read: both turned out to be symptoms of a different, deeper
defect than "corrections can't reach footnote text" -- a misread
footnote digit makes parseFootnotes miss a note boundary and cascade-
merge several notes into one, so the specific footnote each fix would
target (11, and 6's editorial note) no longer exists as its own
addressable definition to correct. That's a structural parsing fix,
not a text substitution -- filed separately as reportsthatmatter-lie,
with both page images' exact readings recorded there.

title: rtm-publish self-publish doesn't reindex search; no staleness alert on search_index_versions
description:
Two related gaps left after reportsthatmatter-7np's fix (per-report scoped reindex, auto-triggered from pnpm publish-report):

1. rtm-publish (@rtm/ingest's report-repo self-publish CLI, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md / AGENTS.md path 1) commits straight to R2+D1 but does not call anything equivalent to scripts/reindex-search.sh. A report published that way can go stale in search with nothing to notice. Fixing this belongs in @rtm/ingest (a separate repo/release), or this repo could poll report_versions and reindex whatever changed.
2. search_index_versions (D1) records which content_version was indexed per report, but nothing reads it back. There is no check anywhere (not verify.sh, not a route) that compares it against a report's actual current content and flags drift.
acceptance_criteria: Either rtm-publish reindexes search itself, or a scheduled/CI check compares search_index_versions against each report's live content_hash/prerendered state and surfaces any report that has drifted (e.g. as a verify.sh check or a /health-style endpoint).
notes:
Addressed the bead's second option (a staleness check), not the first
(rtm-publish reindexing itself) -- that CLI lives in @rtm/ingest, a
separate repo/release, and giving it knowledge of this site's D1/
search infrastructure would cross a boundary the architecture is
deliberately keeping clean (rtm-publish only knows R2 + report_versions).

pnpm check-search-staleness (scripts/check-search-staleness.mjs)
queries remote D1 for report_versions and search_index_versions and
flags any report where indexed_at is older than published_at, or
missing entirely. Deliberately compares timestamps, not the two
tables' content-hash columns -- those are independently-computed
hash schemes (a publish manifest hash vs. a hash over prerendered
section HTML) with no way to compare by value without recomputing
one from the other's inputs, while "was the more recent publish
followed by a reindex" is answerable from timestamps alone and is
exactly the question that matters.

Wired into scripts/verify.sh's VERIFY_BASE (production) branch --
meaningless against local D1, which never carries a real
report_versions row.

Found real drift on its first run: us-911-commission and
us-v-philip-morris were both published before reportsthatmatter-7np/
obw's auto-reindex fix existed, and had never been reindexed since.
Fixed via ./scripts/reindex-search.sh for both; VERIFY_BASE=... ./
scripts/verify.sh now passes clean against production.

title: Address remaining footnote recall and heading-quality cases
description: Work through the bounded ingestion-quality remainder: missing footnote links, PSI truncated headings, and heading ambiguity where it harms a report.
acceptance_criteria: Each adopted fix belongs in the pipeline or report declaration, has a failing case before the fix, passes fidelity and corpus checks after re-ingestion, and has been checked on rendered pages.
notes:
New evidence from reportsthatmatter-axw (2026-09-11): confirmed uk-hillsborough-panel's
footnote-block parser mis-reads its numbered-list citation style ("1. Statement
of... 2. Letter from...", not superscript markers) into a handful of spurious
[^N]: definitions -- not real footnotes. Verified via git-blame that these
definitions predate the axw fix and are unaffected by it; axw's fix just
removed one accidental inline link that had been coincidentally masking the
report's real sidenote count of zero. scripts/verify.sh now carries a
documented carve-out for this report's sidenote-existence check pending a
real fix here -- search it for "uk-hillsborough-panel" to find the exact
failure and the definitions responsible.
2026-09-18 — Challenger evidence from OCR review: printed p. 204 has footnote 63, OCR text 8s Ibid. The footnote parser consumes 8 as the definition identity before corrections run, leaving s Ibid. in note text; a report correction therefore cannot replace the wrong identity with 63. Confirmed against the scan and by an exact-once correction matching zero times. The 8s suspect remains open deliberately. This blocks retiring that single Challenger suspect in reportsthatmatter-agk until footnote identity recovery can handle OCR-confused multi-digit markers.
2026-09-18 follow-up — reportsthatmatter-lie already implemented the relevant recovery in @rtm/ingest v0.12.12, while Challenger is pinned to v0.12.6. The next bounded test is a deliberate ingest dependency bump with a full report/corpus diff; no user input is required.
2026-09-18 correction after read-only validation — current @rtm/ingest v0.12.14 does not solve this page. Running its parser on the real extracted p. 204 lines returns note identities 56, 67, and 8 instead of the scan-confirmed 56–63. A version bump alone is therefore insufficient. Split the precise parser work into reportsthatmatter-aqn and the one-suspect completion into reportsthatmatter-agk.1; aqn blocks agk.1 without blocking the rest of the parent OCR review.
2026-09-20 — Saville Vol I leftovers (also listed on its public PROCESSING.md): 12 of 1,451 notes have no marker in the PDF text layer and appear under 'Notes not linked in the text'; two note rows on p.234 stay plain text because the source numbers two different notes '2'. About 140 mid-sentence paragraph endings are mostly map labels in the PDF text layer and are unlikely to be fixable. The ~50 page-break splits are tracked separately in reportsthatmatter-q0m.

title: Review OCR suspect queues, starting with Challenger
description: Review the 999 open OCR suspects through each report's fidelity workflow. Start with challenger-accident, the largest and messiest queue; record either a deterministic correction or a dismissal so each reviewed suspect leaves the queue permanently.
acceptance_criteria: Review Challenger suspects against the source PDF; record each outcome in the report-owned correction/dismissal data; run the report's prescribed ingestion and fidelity checks; inspect rendered output; leave an updated queue count.
notes:
2026-09-07 — Challenger body pass (PDF pp. 1–200), reviewed against the source scan.

Queue: 371 open → 345 open (7 → 33 judged correct).

corrections.yaml in ../challenger-accident:
- 12 corrections (c-0001..c-0012): 8× 'Recomrnendation/Recornmendat(ion)/Recornmendations' → 'Recommendation(s)' (rn→m OCR of the report's own section headings, narrowed by printed page where the token recurs); 'Cornmission'/'Cornmiasion' → 'Commission' (footnote citations of the Rogers Commission report); 'returnng' → 'returning'; stripped ' lVlll' (mis-OCR of the Contents-page number 'viii').
- 26 dismissals: common English words flagged only for an rn/m sequence (concerns, warning, morning, California, alternatives, preburner(s), …) and two line-break tails already rejoined in the output (cerns→concerns, ternal→External).

Verified: pnpm ingest verify (all fidelity checks green), pnpm ingest check + pnpm ingest baseline challenger-accident (output moved -2 words, baseline accepted), pnpm corpus check (challenger unchanged — no citable id moved), pnpm prerender + grep of rendered HTML (no leftover garble; corrected forms present).

Split out: reportsthatmatter-9zk — the 'Recommendation' headings still merge into the previous paragraph in ~6 places; that's an @rtm/ingest heading-detection bug, not a per-line correction.

Remaining in Challenger (~345): footnote-apparatus garble in pp. 48–200 (mangled footnote numbers / 'Ibid' — 2o, 1bid, 2T, I6Ibid, …), region C appendix prose (pp. 201–260, ~33), region D appendix tables/memos/distribution lists (pp. 261+, ~274 — heavily degraded; many are correct-as-printed alphanumeric part/equipment/document codes). Recommend a dedicated follow-up: a rule/pass to bulk-classify the correct-as-printed codes, then a scoped human pass on what's left, rather than 274 one-off judgements on near-illegible scans. Other reports' queues not yet started.
Corpus blast radius (pnpm corpus check): 9 paragraph permalinks moved in challenger, all direct consequences of the fixes — 'recomrnendation'→'recommendation', '78-rogers-cornmission-report-volume'→'…commission…', 'rogers-cornmiasion-report-volume-i'→'…commission…', and ~5 collision-suffix bumps where the corrected words join an existing 'Recommendation(s)'/'Rogers Commission Report' dedup series. Read the diff; accepted with 'pnpm corpus accept challenger-accident'. ./scripts/verify.sh now exits 0 (All checks passed). challenger-accident is not R2-pinned, and the moved ids were OCR-garble slugs.
2026-09-11 — Challenger footnote-apparatus pass (PDF pp. 48-200 remainder), reviewed against the source scan — several confirmed by rendering the actual page image (pdftoppm), not just the text layer.

Queue: 337 open -> 310 open (41 -> 68 judged correct). Region A (PDF <=47, the Committee's own findings/recommendations) is now fully clear (0 open) after the earlier bookkeeping fix. Region B (footnotes+narrative, 48-200) reduced from 46 to 4 open.

19 corrections (c-0013..c-0033, skipping c-0015/c-0030 — see below): mostly footnote-number reconstructions, verified by bracketing (a garbled number sitting between two clean ones, e.g. '2T'->27 between 26 and 28) or by matching a clean inline citation elsewhere on the page (e.g. 'lZ3Douglas'->123Douglas, matching an already-clean '123' inline). Several needed the actual page image to resolve safely rather than guess: 'lZo'/'lZ4'-family digits are NOT a fixed cipher for this OCR run — '1Z' turned out to be '17' (not '12', my first guess from a wrongly-assumed Z->2 pattern), caught only by rendering the page.

19 dismissals of the newly-corrected match strings (queue bookkeeping — a correction alone never retires a suspect from the queue; see the note above c-0013 in corrections.yaml) + 8 real dismissals (D6AC, 2nd, 1D, 2G, 5B, 6th, 7th — all real words/codes, and '1s' — a Figure VI-2 axis label confirmed '15' against the page image but embedded in an otherwise-illegible ASCII-art diagram).

Real finding: corrections.yaml cannot reach footnote-*definition* text (the rendered '[^N]: ...' blocks) — only body paragraphs/quotes/lists. Confirmed empirically. Two otherwise-solved fixes (footnote 11 '1bid'->'11 Ibid.', and footnote 6's editorial note 'iNm'->'[NOTE.-...]') are left open because of this, both verified correct against the page image but structurally unreachable. Filed as reportsthatmatter-3jb.

Also found and left open: 'lZo' at PDF p.142 sits inside a hyphen-rejoin/footnote-fusion parser bug ('essen-' + the page's footnote text got glued into one fake word 'essenlZo' with no hyphen or space) — a parser issue, not a text correction, in the spirit of reportsthatmatter-9zk. And a THIRD, different 'lZ4' occurrence was spotted in the rendered output (printed p.245-ish, Launch Commit Criteria) that isn't part of this batch's review — left untouched, noted for a future pass.

Verified: pnpm ingest verify (green), pnpm ingest check + baseline (output moved: -1 paragraph/+1 word, from a footnote reference becoming properly linked once its number was fixed; read and accepted), pnpm corpus check + accept (8 paragraph ids moved, all direct/expected consequences, read and accepted), pnpm prerender + grep of rendered HTML (no leftover garble from this batch; corrected forms present). ./scripts/verify.sh green.

Remaining in Challenger (~310): region C appendix prose (~33) and region D appendix tables/memos/distribution lists (~274, mostly correct-as-printed codes per the earlier recommendation) still untouched. Not yet committed to main/published — sitting on local changes pending the user's go-ahead, same as the first batch.
2026-09-13 (backlog audit) — correcting a stale claim above: the 2026-09-11 note says the 41 corrections + queue reduction (337→310 open) were 'sitting on local changes pending the user's go-ahead, not yet committed.' Checked ../challenger-accident directly: that work (through c-0033 in corrections.yaml, commit 56b6d88) plus three follow-on fixes (9zk heading-welding fix, the v0.12.4/v0.12.6 ingest bumps, and a 2026-09-13 footnote-6 recovery fix) are all committed and pushed to origin/main — nothing is pending. fidelity.md currently reads '310 open, 68 reviewed', matching the note's end state exactly. Remaining scope is still region C appendix prose (~33) and region D appendix tables/codes (~274) as previously described; nothing else has changed.
2026-09-18 — Challenger region C prose review (printed pp. 195–251), checked against rendered GPO scan pages.

title: Decide how to handle figures inside page-scanned reports (Challenger, Jack Smith)
description:
Challenger (450 pages) and Jack Smith Vol 1 (174 pages) are page scans: every page is one image, so the embedded-image method does not find figures, and their text is OCR. Decide whether and how to detect a figure region on a scanned page (layout analysis, or a manual list of page regions kept in the report's repo), and whether to publish scans of those regions. Also decide what to do about text that OCR read from within a figure.

Lower priority than the born-digital reports: start only once the pilot (699.1) and survey (699.2) are done.

Acceptance: a written decision on this Bead, and a follow-up Bead per report if the answer is yes.
